names: Thịt ba chỉ rang cháy cạnh
fields: Pork belly with golden-brown edges and clear fat, fragrant with shallots; gently sweet and salty, the lean meat still moist and the edges slightly crisp.
Thịt ba chỉ rang cháy cạnh

Thịt rang cháy cạnh hợp với mâm cơm có cơm nóng, rau và một bát canh nhẹ. Thịt ba chỉ kết hợp với hành tím, được rang để làm nổi vị chính và mùi thơm của phần gia vị đi kèm. Khi đạt, món có mặt thịt nâu nhẹ, phần mỡ trong, vị mặn ngọt và thơm hành. Nêm từng phần giúp giữ vị nguyên liệu rõ hơn. Bày lượng vừa dùng, ăn cùng món có kết cấu khác sẽ khiến bữa cơm hài hòa và dễ ăn.

Serve hot or warm with steamed rice; spoon a little of the sauce over the rice if there is any. The dish is well seasoned, so it usually needs no dipping sauce. Pairs well with: sweet leaf soup with minced pork, boiled morning glory, pickled Vietnamese eggplants.
4 adults; dishes eaten with rice are shared portions in a 3–4 dish meal, noodle/rice/porridge dishes are 4 main portions.
Chuẩn bị là thao tác chủ động; thời gian chờ gồm ướp/ngâm/làm lạnh ngoài thao tác. Tổng theo lịch tuần tự, có thể rút ngắn khi làm song song.
Sweet leaf soup with minced pork
Use a wide pan or heavy-based pot and stir along the bottom so the seasoning does not stick and burn.
Pour off excess fat when needed, keeping just a thin layer so the shallots and seasoning release their aroma.
Add the salty seasoning near the end and stop while still moist; avoid cooking until dry or too salty.
Tender amber pork with clear fat and eggs soaked in colour with rich yolks; a coconut-scented braise, balanced sweet and salty, with no burnt sugar.

Serve hot with rice. Seasoned dishes are eaten as they are; boiled, steamed or lightly fried dishes can use the dipping sauce listed. Add a soup and a vegetable for a complete meal. Pairs well with: tofu in tomato sauce, straw mushroom and tofu soup, salted roasted peanuts.
4 adults; dishes eaten with rice are shared portions in a 3–4 dish meal, noodle/rice/porridge dishes are 4 main portions.
Chuẩn bị là thao tác chủ động; thời gian chờ gồm ướp/ngâm/làm lạnh ngoài thao tác. Tổng theo lịch tuần tự, có thể rút ngắn khi làm song song.
Add vegetables once the water boils, without overcrowding, so it returns to the boil quickly.
Boil stems/roots longer than leaves; test a piece and lift out as soon as tender to keep the crunch.
Transfer to an open plate right away; covering keeps the vegetables cooking and dulls their colour.
Vegetables that keep their colour, crisp-tender and fragrant with garlic.

Plate the greens as soon as the heat is off so the stems stay crisp, scatter the fragrant garlic on top and serve hot. Eat with rice, a savoury dish or tofu and a light soup; do not leave the greens in the hot pan as they soften and lose colour.
4 adults; dishes eaten with rice are shared portions in a 3–4 dish meal, noodle/rice/porridge dishes are 4 main portions.

Drain ingredients well and preheat the pan before adding them to limit liquid release.
Cook in batches if the pan is crowded; a pan that is too cool turns a stir-fry into a stew.

Khi đạt, món có riêu cua đóng mảng, nước thanh và rau không nát. Nêm từng phần giúp giữ vị nguyên liệu rõ hơn. Bày lượng vừa dùng, ăn cùng món có kết cấu khác sẽ khiến bữa cơm hài hòa và dễ ăn.

Ladle out hot with rice and a savoury dish or tofu. No separate dipping sauce is needed; dip the solids only if you like. Pairs well with: caramelised pan-seared pork belly, garlic stir-fried morning glory, pickled Vietnamese eggplants.
4 adults; dishes eaten with rice are shared portions in a 3–4 dish meal, noodle/rice/porridge dishes are 4 main portions.

Strain out shell fragments thoroughly and stir gently before heating; stop stirring once the crab curds start to rise so they clump.
Add hard vegetables first, tender leaves later; add herbs just before turning off the heat.
Taste again once the ingredients release their flavour; add hot water little by little if the soup is too strong.

Bún chả Hà Nội hợp với mâm cơm có cơm nóng, rau và một bát canh nhẹ. Thịt nạc vai xay kết hợp với thịt ba chỉ, được nướng để làm nổi vị chính và mùi thơm của phần gia vị đi kèm. 4 adults; dishes eaten with rice are shared portions in a 3–4 dish meal, noodle/rice/porridge dishes are 4 main portions.

names: Vả trộn hoa màu chay Huế
fields: Miếng vả mềm bùi còn nguyên dạng, quyện vị chua mặn dịu; đậu phụ và nấm làm món thêm chắc vị, rau thơm giữ mùi tươi.
Vả luộc bùi nhẹ trộn cùng đậu phụ, nấm, rau củ và rau thơm; vị chua mặn dịu, ăn kèm bánh tráng giòn theo nếp món chay xứ Huế.
Dùng như món ăn kèm hoặc món trộn chay; xúc bằng bánh tráng. Để riêng bánh tráng, đậu phộng và mè đến lúc dọn.
4 phần ăn kèm; để bánh tráng riêng cho giòn.

Để vả nguội và nguyên liệu ráo trước khi trộn để món không nhão.
Cho nước trộn từng ít một; độ chát và ẩm của quả vả thay đổi theo lứa.

Dọn cơm nóng cùng gà xé, gỏi và chén nước dùng. Nêm nước mắm, tiêu hoặc ớt riêng theo khẩu vị.

Để gà nguội bớt trước khi xé để thớ thịt gọn và không bỏng tay.
Gỏi chỉ trộn rau răm sát lúc ăn để giữ độ tươi.

fields: Thick, chewy rice bánh tằm noodles topped with pork-skin bì tossed in toasted rice powder, boiled pork, fresh vegetables, and gently rich coconut milk. A sweet-salty fish sauce dressing balances this Mekong Delta breakfast.
Bánh tằm bì nước cốt dừa
Serve warm with just enough coconut sauce; keep the fish sauce dressing on the side so everyone can adjust the seasoning.
4 plates of bánh tằm bì with thick noodles, toasted-rice pork skin, and warm coconut milk.

Cut the pork skin into very fine strips so the bì stays tender and mixes easily with the toasted rice powder.

fields: Small rice cakes cooked in individual clay molds until their edges turn golden while the centers stay soft. Shrimp, quail egg, and scallion oil pair with green mango and a hot, savory fish-braising broth in the Phan Rang style.

Serve the cakes hot in small batches with shredded green mango and hot fish-braising broth; fermented fish sauce or chili fish sauce may also be offered.
About 24 small shrimp-and-egg bánh căn, served with hot fish-braising broth.

Resting the batter after mixing lets it hydrate evenly and helps the cakes cook consistently.
Preheat the mold before adding batter and use only a thin coating of oil; bánh căn is cooked in the mold rather than deep-fried.
Cook in small batches and keep the fish-braising broth hot for the local way of serving the cakes.

fields: Small cá linh from the flood season simmered with tart young tamarind, golden sesbania flowers, and rice-paddy herb. The fish tastes naturally sweet, while the flowers add a delicate crunch to this Mekong Delta countryside soup.

4 bowls of soup to share as part of a family rice meal.

names: Buon Ma Thuot red vermicelli soup
ingredients: Ground freshwater crab, strained for broth
fields: Bright orange-red rice vermicelli sits in a tomato-scented freshwater crab broth with crab cake, pork, and Vietnamese basil. The flavor is savory with gentle optional heat.
Red rice vermicelli is served with freshwater crab, tomato, and pork broth in this hearty, familiar Buon Ma Thuot breakfast bowl.
Blanch the noodles and divide them among bowls. Ladle over the broth, crab curds, and pork. Add Vietnamese basil, scallions, roasted peanuts, and chilli to taste; serve hot.
Four generous bowls served as a main dish.

If using ground freshwater crab, strain it twice for a clearer broth.
Cook the crab mixture over low heat and avoid stirring so it sets into soft curds.

Buon Ma Thuot red vermicelli soup

Ivory rice noodles are topped with beef, fried shallots, bean sprouts, and basil. A separate cup of hot broth is served for sipping or pouring as desired.
This Central Highlands specialty is served in two bowls: rice noodles tossed with meat and dark soy sauce, accompanied by a separate cup of clear bone broth.
Divide the noodles among bowls and top with beef, bean sprouts, and basil. Toss with dark soy sauce to taste. Serve with hot broth on the side to sip or add a little at a time.
Four servings, each with a bowl of dry pho and a separate cup of broth.

Blanch the rice noodles just until tender, then drain well so they do not clump.
Keep the broth at a gentle simmer rather than a rolling boil for a clean, clear flavor.
Add the dark soy sauce gradually, as brands vary in saltiness and sweetness.

names: Lotus-seed rice wrapped in lotus leaf
fields: Separate fragrant rice grains mingle with nutty lotus seeds, tofu, mushrooms, and vegetables. The lotus leaf lends a gentle aroma and a characteristic Hue presentation.
Lotus-seed rice wrapped in lotus leaf
Rice mixed with lotus seeds, mushrooms, and vegetables is wrapped in lotus leaf and steamed until lightly fragrant; this family-style vegetarian version is edited by Bếp Việt.
Carefully open the lotus leaf while hot and serve the rice in bowls or directly from the leaf. Pair with lightly spiced soy sauce and simply cooked vegetables.
Four vegetarian portions, served as a main or rice dish in a meat-free meal.

If using dried lotus seeds, soak them for 2–3 hours and boil until tender. Fresh seeds only need the bitter core removed and a brief boil.
Let the rice cool slightly before mixing in the filling so the grains stay intact.
If the lotus leaf is torn, use two layers or steam the rice in a bowl with the leaf laid over it to retain the aroma.

names: Vegetarian grilled eggplant with scallion oil
fields: Tender, juicy eggplant with lightly charred skin absorbs fragrant scallion oil and soy dressing. Roasted peanuts add a nutty finish, making it a good match for hot rice.
Vegetarian grilled eggplant with scallion oil
Tender grilled eggplant is dressed with leek oil and a lightly sweet-sour soy sauce for a simple Vietnamese vegetarian side that is easy to make at home.
Tear or cut the eggplant into bite-size pieces and spoon the soy-and-scallion dressing over it while hot. Sprinkle with peanuts and serve with rice, boiled vegetables, or braised tofu.
Four side portions for a vegetarian meal.

Choose firm, glossy eggplants; grilling them whole helps keep the flesh juicy.
Grill until a chopstick passes through the flesh easily but before it turns mushy; rest for a few minutes before peeling.
Use soy sauce instead of fish sauce to keep the dish fully vegan, and adjust the chilli to taste.

names: Fried tofu with lemongrass and chilli
fields: Golden-edged tofu stays soft inside and is coated with fragrant lemongrass, garlic, and a lightly savory-sweet sauce; red chilli adds gentle heat.
Fried tofu with lemongrass and chilli
Golden tofu is coated with fragrant lemongrass and garlic, seasoned with soy sauce and a little chilli for a quick vegetarian dish suited to everyday rice meals.
Serve the tofu hot with steamed rice, cucumber, or boiled vegetables. Spoon the remaining lemongrass and garlic from the pan over the top for extra aroma.
Four servings with rice for a family vegetarian meal.

Pat the tofu dry before frying so it browns evenly and splatters less.
Drain the lemongrass well and cook over medium-low heat so it turns fragrant without burning or becoming bitter.
Use soy sauce instead of fish sauce, and check packaged seasonings if you need the dish to remain fully vegan.

names: Buon Ma Thuot stacked-plate banh uot
fields: Soft, thin steamed rice sheets are rolled with grilled pork, pork sausage, green mango, cucumber, and herbs. Pineapple fish-paste sauce adds savory, tangy sweetness.
A Buon Ma Thuot specialty of hot steamed rice sheets served on small stacked plates, rolled with grilled meat, sausage, herbs, pickles, and dipping sauce.

Arrange the rice sheets on small plates and stack them. Serve the grilled pork, sausage, herbs, and pickles separately so everyone can roll their own; offer pineapple fish-paste sauce or sweet-sour fish sauce.
Four servings, about 12 small plates of thin steamed rice sheets for rolling with meat, sausage, and vegetables.

If using chilled rice sheets, re-steam each portion for 1–2 minutes until soft and hot.
Slice the pork evenly and thinly so it cooks quickly; grill just until done to keep it juicy.
Gradually mix the fermented fish sauce with pineapple and warm water, tasting as you go because saltiness varies by brand.
Buon Ma Thuot stacked-plate banh uot
Shiitake and straw mushrooms turn tender in a glossy brown soy sauce with black pepper and leek. The braising sauce is lightly thickened and not overly salty.
Fresh mushrooms are braised in a claypot with soy sauce, pepper, and a little coconut water until flavorful and glossy, making a vegetarian dish to serve with hot rice.
Serve hot in the claypot or transfer to a small plate, then top with scallions and pepper. Pair with rice, boiled vegetables, or a light soup.
Four servings with rice for a family vegetarian meal.

Wipe the mushrooms with a damp cloth or rinse quickly, then drain well so they do not release too much water.
Braise over low heat and gently shake the pot instead of stirring hard so the mushrooms keep their shape.
Season with soy sauce gradually; if the pot reduces too quickly, add 1–2 tablespoons of hot water.
Fluffy grains are lightly seasoned with soy sauce and dotted with orange carrot, yellow corn, green peas, and red pepper. Mushrooms and tofu add savory depth.
Cold rice is stir-fried until fluffy with tofu, mushrooms, and colorful vegetables for a quick vegetarian meal using everyday ingredients.

Four plates of fried rice served as the main dish in a vegetarian meal.

Use cooled rice with a dry surface so the grains stay separate rather than clumping.

Fry the rice in batches that fit the pan; an overcrowded pan steams the rice and makes it soft.
Soft rice grains remain visible in this gentle mushroom congee, topped with scallions, cilantro, pepper, and a touch of sesame oil; it is best served hot.
Rice is simmered until soft with shiitake and straw mushrooms, then lightly seasoned with soy sauce for a comforting vegetarian breakfast that is easy to prepare.
Ladle the hot congee into bowls and top with scallions, cilantro, and pepper. Serve soy sauce or chilli on the side for seasoning to taste.

Stir the bottom of the pot often toward the end so the congee does not stick.
Add the mushrooms after the rice has expanded so they retain their natural sweetness and are not overcooked.

names: Stir-fried noodles with mushrooms and tofu
fields: Chewy golden noodles are lightly coated in soy sauce and tossed with green bok choy, fragrant mushrooms, crisp carrot, and pan-seared tofu.

Four plates of stir-fried noodles served as a main dish.

Blanch the noodles until just tender, rinse briefly with cool water, drain, and toss with a little oil to prevent sticking.
Stir-fry the vegetables over high heat, adding the ones that take longest to cook first.

A clear broth fragrant with star anise and cinnamon draws natural sweetness from vegetables. Soft pho noodles, golden tofu, mushrooms and fresh cilantro make a light yet satisfying bowl.
Phở chay dùng nước dùng rau củ ninh cùng gừng và gia vị phở, ăn với bánh phở, đậu phụ, nấm và rau thơm.
Blanch the pho noodles, add tofu and mushrooms, then ladle over hot broth. Finish with spring onion and cilantro; serve with bean sprouts, lime and chili on the side.
Four hot bowls of pho with rice noodles, tofu, mushrooms and aromatic vegetable broth.

If using dried pho noodles, soak and blanch them according to the package directions so they soften without turning mushy.

Split each baguette lengthwise and spread with a thin layer of vegan sauce if desired. Add the tofu, drained pickles, cucumber and cilantro; serve while the bread is crisp.
Four vegetarian baguettes filled with pan-seared tofu, pickled vegetables, cucumber and cilantro.

Pat the tofu dry before pan-frying so it browns evenly and splatters less.

Four bowls of vegetarian bun rieu with soy curds, tofu, mushrooms, tomato and fresh greens.

names: Vung Tau bánh khọt mini pancakes
fields: Each little cake has a crisp golden base, a soft coconut-scented center and a sweet shrimp on top. Scallion oil, fresh greens, pickles and sweet-sour fish sauce keep the flavors bright.

names: Black carp braised with galangal and fermented crab sauce
fields: The carp steaks hold their shape while becoming tender and firm, coated in a deep amber-brown sauce. Galangal and ginger add warmth, fermented crab sauce brings savory depth, and lime balances the fish.

Four portions of black carp braised in a clay pot with galangal, ginger, lime, fish sauce and fermented crab sauce.

names: Cassava bánh tằm with coconut milk
fields: Translucent cassava strands are soft and chewy, coated with fresh coconut and a lightly savory-sweet coconut sauce. Toasted sesame and crushed peanuts add a nutty finish to this comforting market treat.

A southern Vietnamese market cake made from grated cassava, squeezed and steamed into chewy translucent strands, served with grated coconut, coconut milk, sesame and peanuts.
Cut the cake into short strands, roll gently in grated coconut and plate. Drizzle with warm coconut sauce, sprinkle with toasted sesame and crushed peanuts, and serve the same day while chewy.
Four plates of chewy cassava bánh tằm topped with grated coconut and lightly sweetened coconut milk.

Bánh tẻ làng Chờ có vỏ bột gạo dẻo giòn, nhân thịt, mộc nhĩ, hành và tiêu, gói thon trong lá dong. Bản gia đình dùng bột gạo xay sẵn để rút ngắn thời gian ngâm gạo truyền thống.
Unwrap the cakes while warm and serve with lightly seasoned fish sauce, or enjoy them plain to appreciate the rice and dong-leaf aroma. Best eaten the same day.
Eight small rice cakes, two per person; serve warm with lightly seasoned fish sauce.
Editorial time estimate; actual time depends on the equipment, ingredients and cooking experience.
bánh gạo nhân thịt mộc nhĩ
Stir the batter continuously over low heat so it thickens evenly without lumps or sticking.
Use just enough filling and seal both ends so the cakes do not split while steaming.
The traditional method soaks and wet-grinds rice over a longer period; this version is shortened by using ready-milled rice flour.

The porridge is thick, with tender rice grains that still hold their shape. Turmeric eel is savory and warmly fragrant with Vietnamese shallots; Vietnamese coriander, pepper and scallions add a fresh finish.
Cháo lươn Vinh nổi bật với lươn xào riêng cùng nghệ, ớt và hành tăm, đặt trên cháo gạo tẻ ninh mềm từ nước dùng. Bát cháo nóng thường rắc rau răm, hành và tiêu.
Ladle the hot porridge into bowls and top with the fried eel, Vietnamese coriander, scallions and pepper. Serve with steamed rice sheets or bread, adding chili to taste.
Four bowls of medium-thick rice porridge topped with turmeric eel, Vietnamese shallots, chili and Vietnamese coriander.
Editorial time estimate; actual time depends on the equipment, ingredients and cooking experience.
If buying live eel, ask the seller to clean it. Remove the slime and cook it thoroughly; keep raw-eel utensils separate from the greens.
Cook the whole rice grains until soft and expanded; do not blend them, to retain Vinh-style porridge texture.
Stir-fry the eel separately with turmeric and Vietnamese shallots, then add it to the bowl just before serving to preserve its aroma.
The chicken is firm on the outside, tender and juicy within, infused with turmeric and Vietnamese shallots. The lightly golden broth carries lime-leaf aroma; taro stems add a tender, crisp bite.
Xáo gà Thanh Chương nấu gà miếng với hành tăm, nghệ, lá chanh và muối; nước xáo vàng thơm, dùng nóng với cơm, bún hoặc bánh mướt. Bản gia đình thêm dọc mùng đã sơ chế kỹ.
Ladle the chicken and broth into bowls, then garnish with finely sliced lime leaves and Vietnamese coriander. Serve hot with rice, fresh rice vermicelli or steamed rice sheets.
Four portions of Thanh Chuong chicken stew, served with rice, rice vermicelli or steamed rice sheets.
Editorial time estimate; actual time depends on the equipment, ingredients and cooking experience.
món gà ăn với bánh mướt
Start over low heat to sear the chicken gently and draw out its flavor before adding water; avoid high-heat frying.
Peel the taro stems, massage with salt, rinse and squeeze dry. If they still cause irritation, blanch briefly before cooking.
Local sources describe seasoning with salt instead of fish sauce to preserve the chicken and Vietnamese shallot aroma.

names: Sợi bánh cháo canh xứ Nghệ
fields: The noodles are pleasantly chewy and soak up the lightly thickened, gently sweet bone broth. Pork, shrimp, scallions and fried shallots add savory depth; chili or lime gives the bowl a warming finish.
Sợi bánh cháo canh xứ Nghệ
Cháo canh Nghệ An không phải cháo gạo: sợi bột mì pha một phần bột gạo được cán cắt thủ công, nấu lại trong nước dùng xương có độ sánh. Tô ăn kèm thịt, chả hoặc tôm tùy nơi.
Ladle the hot noodles and broth into bowls, then add pork, shrimp, scallions, fried shallots and pepper. Serve with chili paste and lime if desired.
Four bowls of wheat-and-rice noodles in lightly thickened bone broth with pork and shrimp.
Editorial time estimate; actual time depends on the equipment, ingredients and cooking experience.
Roll the dough to a moderate thickness and dust lightly with flour so the noodles do not stick when cut.
Blanch the noodles, briefly rinse them in cold water, then cook them again to keep them springy and separate.
The broth should be slightly thick. Simmer the noodles in it for a few minutes for the characteristic texture, stirring gently.

names: Son La Pa Pinh Top Grilled Fish
Cá nướng mắc khén Sơn La
fields: Tender fish scented with lemongrass and herbs, lightly charred outside with the warm, citrusy tingle of mak khen pepper.
Cá nướng mắc khén Sơn La

Pa pinh top is a Thai dish from Son La: fresh fish seasoned with herbs and mak khen, folded and grilled. Bep Viet has adapted a home-cooking version using cleaned carp or stream fish, grilled over charcoal or in an oven.
Transfer the hot fish to a platter, lift off the flesh and serve with sticky or steamed rice. Add boiled greens and cham cheo dipping sauce if desired.
One 1–1.2 kg stream fish or carp, stuffed with herbs and grilled folded; share with sticky rice or steamed rice.
Thời lượng tham khảo; kích thước cá và thiết bị nướng ảnh hưởng thời gian chín.
Son La Pa Pinh Top Grilled Fish
Choose fresh fish and make shallow cuts through the thickest parts so the seasoning penetrates while the fish stays intact.
Mak khen is potent; toast it lightly, crush it and add a little at a time so it does not overpower the fish.
For oven cooking, roast at 200°C and make sure the flesh next to the bone is fully cooked before serving.

names: Vịt quay lá mắc mật Xứ Lạng
fields: Golden-brown duck skin fragrant with honey and mac mat; tender meat seasoned with fermented soybean and garlic, best served freshly carved.
Vịt quay lá mắc mật Xứ Lạng

Lang Son roast duck is seasoned inside with mac mat leaves and fruit, fermented soybean paste, soy sauce and garlic, then glazed with honey. Bep Viet adapts the traditional roast for a home oven while keeping its mac mat aroma and glossy golden skin.
Carve the duck into serving pieces and pair with hot rice, pickles or boiled greens. Spoon over thoroughly boiled roasting juices for a richer taste.
One 1.8–2 kg duck, carved into pieces to share at the table.
Thời lượng tham khảo gồm ướp lạnh; thời gian quay thay đổi theo kích thước vịt và thiết bị.
Pat the duck skin completely dry and leave it uncovered in the refrigerator for a few hours before roasting.
If mac mat fruit is unavailable, add a little more of the leaves; avoid substituting a large amount of another aromatic spice.
Use a food thermometer to check that the thickest part of the thigh reaches at least 74°C; rest the duck before carving.
Warm, tender rice cakes carry the fragrance of rice and water celery; sweet shrimp balances the tangy-sweet fish sauce and pickles.

Shrimp rice pancakes are a familiar Thanh Hoa afternoon snack. Rice-flour batter is poured into small pancakes with tiny shrimp, water celery and cabbage; this Bep Viet version keeps those simple ingredients.
Serve the pancakes as soon as they are cooked, with sweet-and-sour fish sauce and pickles. Cut into small bites with chopsticks.
About 12 small pancakes, served hot with sweet-and-sour fish sauce and pickled vegetables.
Thời lượng tham khảo; số bánh mỗi mẻ tùy kích thước chảo.
Stir the batter before each pour because rice flour settles easily.
Spread the batter in a moderately thin layer so it cooks evenly; the pancake does not need to be very crisp.
Dried shrimp can replace fresh shrimp; briefly soak and drain it very well before adding it to the pan.

names: Cao Bang Rice Rolls in Pork Broth
fields: Soft, slightly chewy rice rolls hold fragrant pork filling; clear, hot pork broth is finished with fried shallots and cilantro.

Cao Bang rice rolls are served hot with bone broth instead of the fish-sauce dip found elsewhere. This version uses thin rice sheets, minced pork and wood-ear mushroom filling, and hot broth; egg can be cooked into the roll as it is locally.
Arrange the rolls in bowls, ladle over hot pork broth and add fried shallots, cilantro and pepper. Serve with egg rice rolls or Vietnamese pork sausage if desired.
Four bowls of hot rice rolls with pork-bone broth, minced pork and optional egg cooked into the rolls.
Thời lượng bao gồm ngâm gạo/bột; thời gian tráng phụ thuộc dụng cụ và số mẻ.
Cao Bang Rice Rolls in Pork Broth
Soak the rice thoroughly and grind it finely. If using ready-made rice flour, add water gradually until it is thin enough to spread.
Keep the broth at a gentle simmer and skim off foam to keep it clear.
For egg rolls, spread a thin layer of egg over the nearly cooked rice sheet and roll it once the egg sets.

names: Chả ram tôm đất Quy Nhơn
fields: Crisp, thin rice-paper wrappers enclose sweet shrimp and gently rich pork; fresh greens make each hot bite feel lighter.
Chả ram tôm đất Quy Nhơn

Binh Dinh land-shrimp rolls wrap small sweet shrimp and pork belly in thin rice paper and fry them until golden. Bep Viet keeps the filling simple so the shrimp stands out, serving fresh greens and sweet-sour fish sauce on the side.
Arrange the hot ram rolls on a plate and serve with fresh herbs, mustard greens and sweet-and-sour fish sauce or chili sauce.
About 20 small ram rolls to share with fresh herbs and dipping sauce.
Thời lượng tham khảo; lượng dầu thực tế thay đổi theo kích thước chảo và cách chiên.
chả ram tôm đất Bình Định
chả ram tôm đất Quy Nhơn
Drain the filling before rolling so the rice paper does not become wet and split during frying.
Roll snugly and place the seam side down in the pan first to help each roll hold its shape.
Fry in small batches over medium heat, then drain on a rack to keep the wrappers crisp.

names: Spicy fish noodle soup, Hải Phòng style
fields: The clear broth is savory from the bones, gently sour from tamarind and fragrant with mild chili. Golden fried fish keeps its flaky texture alongside soft noodles and crisp elephant ear stem.

Hải Phòng spicy fish noodles pair a clear bone broth, colored with tomato and chili, with turmeric-seasoned fried tilapia, fish cake, elephant ear stem and rice vermicelli. Bếp Việt has adapted a home-cooking version with adjustable heat.

Blanch the noodles, arrange the fried fish, fish cake and elephant ear stem in bowls, then ladle over hot broth. Serve with fresh herbs, banana blossom and chili sauce so everyone can adjust the heat.
Four bowls of noodles with fried tilapia, fish cake, elephant ear stem and tangy, mildly spicy tomato broth.
Thời gian ninh tùy loại xương; cá cần được nấu chín hoàn toàn.
Spicy fish noodle soup, Hải Phòng style
Pat the fish completely dry before coating it so the crust turns crisp and the oil does not splatter.
Blanch the elephant ear stem with a little salt, rinse and gently squeeze to reduce irritation.
Add tamarind and chili gradually; the sour, spicy notes should lift the bone broth without overpowering the fish.

names: Hải Phòng square crab spring rolls
fields: Crisp golden rice-paper wrappers enclose sweet crab, tender glass noodles and a well-seasoned filling; garlic-lime dipping sauce balances the richness.

Nem cua bể is Hải Phòng’s palm-sized square spring roll. Its filling combines sea crab, pork, glass noodles, wood ear and shiitake mushrooms, egg and vegetables. Bếp Việt has adapted the square-folding and frying method for home kitchens.
Serve whole or halved while hot, with rice vermicelli, lettuce, herbs and sweet-and-sour fish sauce.
Eight square rolls served with fresh rice vermicelli, herbs and sweet-and-sour fish sauce.
Thời gian chiên tùy độ dày nem và nhiệt dầu; nhân cần nóng chín đều trước khi dùng.
Hải Phòng square crab spring rolls
Drain the noodles, mushrooms and vegetables well before mixing so the wrappers stay crisp.
Do not overfill or wrap too tightly; seal the square edges so the filling stays inside while frying.
Fry over medium heat and turn evenly so the filling heats through before the wrapper gets too dark.

names: Huế bánh nậm wrapped in banana leaves
fields: The cake is soft and smooth with a gentle banana-leaf aroma; a thin line of shrimp and pork filling brings mild savory-sweet flavor and a touch of pepper.
Huế bánh nậm wrapped in banana leaves

Huế bánh nậm has a soft rice-flour layer spread thinly on banana or dong leaves, topped with shrimp and pork sautéed with shallots. Bếp Việt has adapted a thin-wrapped version, gently steamed and served with mild chili fish sauce.
Unwrap while warm, scoop up each soft bite and dip it in fish sauce diluted with sugar, lime and chili.
About 16 thin banana-leaf-wrapped rice cakes, steamed and served with chili fish sauce.
Thời gian hấp tùy độ dày bánh và số lượng trong xửng; xếp bánh cách nhau để hơi lưu thông.
bánh bột gạo nhân tôm thịt
Stir the batter over low heat until just thick enough to coat a spoon; it should remain smooth and spreadable.
Cook the filling until its moisture evaporates before spreading it on the batter; this helps the cakes hold their flat shape while steaming.
Brush the leaves lightly with oil and use a thin layer of batter to keep the cakes soft and flat.

names: Hội An stir-fried clams with rice crackers
Hoi An stir-fried clams with rice crackers
Hoi An clams with rice crackers
fields: Small clams are tender and sweet, fragrant with shallots, garlic and Vietnamese coriander, with a nutty finish from peanuts. Crisp rice crackers add contrast.
Hoi An stir-fried clams with rice crackers
Hoi An clams with rice crackers

Hến xào xúc bánh tráng is a familiar Hội An dish: small clams quickly stir-fried with shallots, garlic, Vietnamese coriander and seasonings, then scooped with crisp rice crackers. Bếp Việt adds roasted peanuts and a moderate amount of chili for a nutty, aromatic home-cooking version.
Serve the hot clams in a shallow dish, topped with peanuts and Vietnamese coriander. Break the rice crackers into scoop-sized pieces; sweet-and-sour fish sauce is optional.
One sharing plate of stir-fried clams for four, served with toasted rice crackers for scooping.
Không tính thời gian đãi hến nếu mua nguyên vỏ; hến phải được làm sạch cát và nấu chín trước khi dùng.
Hội An stir-fried clams with rice crackers
If using live clams in their shells, rinse thoroughly, boil just until they open, remove the meat and drain well before stir-frying.
Stir-fry the clams briefly over high heat to preserve their sweetness and prevent excess liquid.
Add the Vietnamese coriander at the end and sprinkle on the peanuts just before serving.
Chewy, earthy cassava meets lightly rich coconut, crunchy roasted peanuts and a touch of salt that brings out its gentle sweetness.

Hội An bánh sắn đập is made by pounding chewy cassava flat rather than mashing it, steaming it with grated coconut and finishing with roasted peanuts. Bếp Việt has adapted a home version with careful soaking and thorough cooking, preserving its earthy, lightly rich character.
Arrange the warm cakes on a plate, top with grated coconut and crushed roasted peanuts, and add a pinch of salted sugar if desired.
About eight chewy steamed cassava pieces topped with grated coconut and roasted peanuts, best served warm.
Tổng thời gian gồm 30 phút ngâm; thời gian hấp thay đổi theo độ dày miếng sắn. Sắn phải được sơ chế và nấu chín hoàn toàn.
steamed cassava with coconut and peanuts
Choose fresh, white-fleshed cassava with few fibers; remove the thick skin, pink inner layer and central woody core.
Soak the cassava in clean water for at least 30 minutes and discard the water. Steam until fully tender; never eat it undercooked.
Pound the cassava just enough to flatten it while keeping the fibers intact; do not mash it into a paste.
Crisp rice crackers sandwich a soft rice sheet, served with pineapple, garlic and chili mam nem.

In Cam Nam, banh dap pairs a soft steamed rice sheet between crisp rice crackers, broken by hand and dipped in mam nem. Bep Viet has adapted the local combination for home cooking, keeping the dipping sauce separate so each person can adjust it.
Serve as soon as assembled so the crackers stay crisp. Keep the mam nem dip separate and serve with herbs and cucumber.
Four portions of crisp rice crackers layered with soft steamed rice sheets and pineapple mam nem.
Assemble the toasted rice crackers and steamed sheets close to serving so the crackers stay crisp.
Let the rice sheets cool and dry slightly before assembling so the crackers do not soften too quickly.
Toast the rice crackers over low heat, turning frequently until crisp and puffed without scorching.
Season the mam nem gradually because saltiness varies by brand.

names: Da Nang vermicelli with pork and fermented fish sauce
Da Nang vermicelli with fermented anchovy sauce
Bún mắm thịt luộc Đà Nẵng
fields: A dry noodle bowl with fragrant roast pork, tender young jackfruit, crisp greens and gently spicy pineapple mam nem, finished with roasted peanuts.
Da Nang vermicelli with fermented anchovy sauce
Bún mắm thịt luộc Đà Nẵng

Da Nang bun mam is a dry vermicelli dish with pork, young jackfruit, fresh greens, pickled papaya, peanuts and fermented fish sauce. Bep Viet uses ready-cooked roast pork for a quicker meal and balances the savory sauce with pineapple.
Arrange the vermicelli, pork, jackfruit, pickled papaya, greens and cucumber in bowls. Add just enough mam nem, top with peanuts and toss just before eating.
Four bowls of dry vermicelli with roast pork, young jackfruit, fresh greens, pickled papaya and fermented fish sauce.
This quick version uses fully cooked roast pork and is served without broth.
Da Nang vermicelli with pork and fermented fish sauce
Add the mam nem a little at a time, tasting it with the noodles and greens to avoid over-seasoning.
If using boiled young jackfruit, drain it well and tear it into bite-sized pieces.
Store purchased roast pork safely in the refrigerator and reheat it thoroughly before serving.
Hot, lightly golden tapioca cakes wrap a chewy pork-and-egg filling; fresh herbs and pickled papaya balance each bite.

Thuan An pressed cakes have a thin, chewy tapioca wrapper cooked with pork, egg and scallions; they can be served soft or pressed until drier. Bep Viet has adapted the method for a home griddle or press and serves them with fresh herbs, pickles and dipping sauce.
Eat while hot, wrapped or served with fresh herbs and pickled papaya; dip in a lightly diluted chili fish sauce.
Four portions of tapioca cakes filled with pork and egg, served with herbs, pickles and a mildly spicy dip.
The amount of water depends on the starch; add boiling water gradually and stop once the dough is pliable.
Knead while the water is still hot, but let it cool enough to handle. Add it gradually until the dough is pliable, not sticky.
Press the cakes thinly and spread the filling evenly so the dough cooks through before the surface darkens.
Adjust crispness by changing the pressing time; avoid drying the cakes so much that they become hard.
Golden patties with a tender, springy squid-and-pork center, served on sugarcane sticks for a subtle sweetness.

Ha Lung cha chia combines pounded squid and pork molded around sugarcane, bringing savory seafood flavor and a gentle sweetness. For this small home batch, Bep Viet steams the patties to keep them moist, then lightly sears them for a golden surface.
Serve hot with fresh herbs and chili fish sauce. Hold by the sugarcane stick, or remove it before serving to young children.
Four servings of squid-and-pork patties molded around sugarcane, steamed and lightly seared in Bep Viet's home adaptation.
Steaming cooks the pork and squid evenly; the quick sear is only for color and aroma.
Use fresh, well-drained squid and pound or pulse until tacky; avoid over-processing, which can warm the mixture.
Mold a moderate layer of mixture around the sugarcane so the center cooks evenly.
Steam the patties through before searing briefly; make sure the center is fully cooked before serving.
A chewy black ramie and glutinous-rice wrapper surrounds a fragrant mung-bean and coconut filling with sweetened pork fat and candied winter melon.

Ninh Giang banh gai are known for their glossy, chewy black glutinous-rice wrapper colored with ramie leaves. The filling combines mung beans, coconut, sweetened pork fat and candied winter melon, wrapped in dried banana leaves. Bep Viet has edited a small-batch method while retaining these signature ingredients and noting the soaking and steaming time.
Let the cakes cool slightly after steaming, then unwrap the banana leaves and serve as a snack or edible gift. Keep leftovers wrapped to preserve freshness.
Eight ramie-leaf sticky-rice cakes filled with mung beans, coconut, sweetened pork fat and candied winter melon, wrapped in banana leaves and steamed.
The rice and mung beans need advance soaking; allow about 6 hours of hands-off time, not including cooling.
Soak the glutinous rice long enough to hydrate evenly, then drain it thoroughly before grinding or pounding.
Boil the ramie leaves until tender, remove tough veins and pound or blend until smooth for a silky wrapper.
Steam until the wrappers are evenly chewy; timing depends on cake size and how tightly the steamer is covered.
A bowl of clear, lightly fragrant fish broth with tender mackerel, springy fish cake, greens and a little lime and chili.

Nha Trang fish-cake vermicelli is known for a clear, delicate broth made from sea-fish heads and bones, served with fish pieces and steamed or fried fish cakes. Bep Viet has edited a home-sized recipe, simmering gently and adding a measured amount of fermented shrimp paste to preserve the fish's natural sweetness.
Blanch the noodles, arrange the mackerel and fish cakes in bowls, then ladle over the hot broth. Serve with fresh greens, banana blossom, lime and chili.
Four bowls of clear fish broth with fish pieces, steamed and fried fish cakes, and fresh greens.
Use no pork bones; simmer the broth from marine fish heads and bones.
Briefly blanch and rinse the fish bones to keep the broth clear and reduce fishy aromas.
Maintain a gentle simmer and avoid stirring the fish bones vigorously.
Add strained fermented shrimp paste gradually; saltiness and aroma vary by brand.

names: Bánh căn xíu mại Đà Lạt
fields: Small cakes with crisp golden edges and soft egg-and-shrimp toppings, served with hot tomato pork meatballs and shredded papaya.
Bánh căn xíu mại Đà Lạt

Da Lat banh can are small rice-flour cakes cooked in individual clay molds until their edges turn crisp, traditionally served with dipping sauce, often tomato pork meatballs and shredded papaya. Bep Viet has adapted the dish for a home banh can pan or dimpled skillet, with quail egg and shrimp toppings.
Arrange the hot cakes on a plate and serve with tomato pork meatballs, shredded papaya and herbs. Dip each cake into the sauce before eating.
Four servings of small rice cakes topped with egg and shrimp, served with tomato pork meatballs and shredded papaya.
If using a cast-iron pan instead of a clay mold, adjust the heat so the cakes cook through before their edges become too dark.
Rest the batter after mixing so the rice flour hydrates and the cakes cook evenly.
Preheat the molds before pouring in the batter; brush with only a thin film of oil for crisp edges.
Cook the pork meatballs through and keep the sauce hot for serving.

names: Gỏi củ hũ dừa xứ dừa
fields: Crisp, cool coconut-heart strips pair with soft tofu, crunchy tofu skin, fragrant Vietnamese coriander and a gentle sweet-sour dressing.
Gỏi củ hũ dừa xứ dừa

Coconut heart, the crisp, mildly sweet core of the palm, is closely associated with Ben Tre's coconut-growing region. This vegan salad combines it with tofu, tofu skin, Vietnamese coriander, peanuts and a sweet-sour dressing. Bep Viet uses soy sauce, lime and sugar instead of fish sauce to keep the dish fully plant-based.
Toss the salad shortly before serving. Plate it and top with peanuts, crisp tofu skin and vegan fried shallots. Serve any extra dressing on the side.
Four plant-based servings of crisp coconut heart, tofu, tofu skin, Vietnamese coriander and peanuts.
Choose soy sauce, tofu skin, and fried shallots made entirely from plant-based ingredients to keep the dish vegetarian.
After slicing, soak the coconut heart in ice water with lime to preserve its pale color and crisp texture.
Dry the coconut heart and greens thoroughly before tossing so the salad does not become watery.
Check the tofu-skin and fried-shallot labels to ensure they contain no animal-derived additives.

names: Lai Thieu chicken and mangosteen salad
Gỏi gà măng cụt Bình Dương
fields: Tender shredded chicken, crisp mildly tart young mangosteen, cool vegetables, fragrant Vietnamese coriander and roasted peanuts.
Gỏi gà măng cụt Bình Dương

Lai Thieu chicken and mangosteen salad is associated with the season for young mangosteen: firm chicken is tossed with crisp, mildly tart fruit, onion, Vietnamese coriander and peanuts. Bep Viet has edited a home-sized method, peeling the fruit under running water and soaking it in salted lime water to reduce sap and preserve its color.
Toss the salad just before serving and top with peanuts and fried shallots. Serve with prawn crackers or use the chicken broth to make a side porridge.
Four servings of shredded chicken salad with young mangosteen, onion, carrot, Vietnamese coriander, peanuts and sweet-sour fish sauce.
Green mangosteen is seasonal; 2 kg of whole fruit usually yields only about 400–500 g of edible flesh for the salad.
Lai Thieu chicken and mangosteen salad
Choose green or just-yellow mangosteens with firm flesh; ripe, soft fruit can break apart when tossed.
Wear gloves while peeling mangosteen under running water, then immediately soak the flesh in cold salted lime water to reduce sap and browning.
Poach the chicken until fully cooked, cool it promptly and refrigerate it if you will not toss the salad right away.

names: Vegan straw mushrooms braised with pepper
Nấm rơm kho tiêu xanh chay
fields: Plump straw mushrooms in a lightly reduced soy glaze, warmly scented with green peppercorns and gently sweet.
Nấm rơm kho tiêu xanh chay

Vegan straw mushrooms braised with pepper make a simple rice-table dish: plump mushrooms are simmered with soy sauce, green peppercorns and a little caramel until lightly glazed. Bep Viet has edited a fully plant-based version, using leek instead of shallot or garlic and omitting fish sauce.
Serve hot with steamed rice and boiled greens. Add ground pepper or a few slices of chili for more heat.
Four servings of straw mushrooms braised with green peppercorns, served with rice and boiled vegetables.
This is fully plant-based; use leek and check the caramel sauce and soy sauce ingredients if strict vegan preparation is required.
Vegan straw mushrooms braised with pepper
Rinse the mushrooms quickly, drain them well and braise over medium heat so they do not release too much liquid.
Season with soy sauce first, then taste before adding salt because saltiness varies by brand.
Choose plant-based caramel coloring and soy sauce.

names: Gỏi cá mai Bà Rịa - Vũng Tàu
fields: Pearly white fish lightly coated with fragrant toasted rice powder, fresh herbs, shallots and roasted peanuts, balanced by a tangy, creamy peanut dip.
Gỏi cá mai Bà Rịa - Vũng Tàu

This coastal salad balances the delicate sweetness of small sea fish with lime, toasted rice powder, fresh herbs and roasted peanuts. Bep Viet has adapted the preparation for a family-sized batch, keeping the fish chilled throughout and serving it with a lightly thickened peanut sauce.
Arrange the fish and herbs on a chilled plate and serve immediately with rice paper and dipping sauce. Keep any unused portion refrigerated; do not leave it at room temperature.
Four servings of mackerel scad salad with toasted rice powder, herbs, roasted peanuts and a rich dipping sauce.
This salad uses raw fish briefly marinated in an acidic dressing; keep it chilled and serve immediately after mixing.
Buy very fresh fish from a trusted supplier and keep it chilled throughout; lime and vinegar do not replace safe handling of raw fish.
Add the toasted rice powder and herbs just before serving so the fish does not release excess liquid and the herbs stay crisp.
Taste the sauce after heating and add water if it is too thick.

names: Quang Ngai tuna um noodle soup
Bún cá ngừ um miền Trung
fields: A hot bowl of vermicelli with tender tuna, softened tomatoes and pineapple in a lightly golden broth, served with fresh greens and a little chili.
Bún cá ngừ um miền Trung

This central Vietnamese noodle soup features seared tuna gently braised with tomatoes, pineapple and spices for a full-flavored broth with natural sweet-and-sour notes. Bep Viet has adapted it for a family pot so the fish cooks tender while holding its shape.
Blanch the vermicelli, arrange the fish and greens in bowls, and ladle over the hot broth. Serve with fresh greens, lime and chili to taste.
Four bowls of vermicelli with tender braised tuna, tomato, pineapple and a mildly spicy broth.
The tuna is seared and then gently braised so it absorbs the seasoning without falling apart.
Quang Ngai tuna um noodle soup
Pat the tuna very dry before searing so its surface firms up and the pieces hold together while braising.
Braise the fish gently and avoid stirring; check doneness according to the thickness of the slices.
Add boiling water for a lighter broth, then adjust the seasoning.
A glossy green plate of just-cooked fiddlehead ferns with lightly crisp shoots, fragrant garlic and little excess liquid.

Fiddlehead fern is a wild mountain vegetable that grows in cool, damp places; its young curled shoots have a distinctive crisp texture. Bep Viet quickly stir-fries it with garlic and plant-based seasonings for a fresh, green side dish.
Serve the fern as soon as it is stir-fried, alongside hot rice and other savory or vegetarian dishes.
Four servings of fiddlehead ferns quickly stir-fried with garlic to retain their green color and light crunch.
Blanch and stir-fry briefly to preserve the fern's green color and light crunch.
Choose tender young shoots, discard old leaves and rinse several times to remove grit.
Blanch the fern briefly and drain before stir-frying to shorten its time in the pan.
Stir-fry in small batches over high heat and use just enough soy sauce to keep the fern from releasing water.

names: Mang Den grilled chicken with bamboo sticky rice
Cơm lam gà nướng Tây Nguyên
fields: Golden, lemongrass-fragrant chicken with juicy meat, paired with chewy bamboo sticky rice and nutty sesame-peanut salt.
Cơm lam gà nướng Tây Nguyên

Grilled chicken with cơm lam is a familiar highland pairing: fragrant marinated chicken cooked over coals alongside sticky rice steamed in bamboo. Bep Viet has adapted it for home cooking with free-range chicken, aromatic é basil and flexible oven or charcoal methods.
Cut the chicken into pieces, remove the sticky rice from its bamboo tubes and slice it. Serve with sesame-peanut salt, é basil and fresh greens.
Four servings of golden-skinned grilled chicken with bamboo-cooked sticky rice and sesame-peanut salt.
Roasting time varies with the chicken's size and oven; make sure it is fully cooked before serving.
Mang Den grilled chicken with bamboo sticky rice
Soak the sticky rice long enough and drain it so it cooks evenly in the bamboo.
When roasting in an oven, turn the chicken halfway through and check that the thickest part reaches at least 74°C.
Rest the chicken for 10 minutes after roasting before carving to retain its juices.

names: Bánh tét đậu xanh dừa chay
fields: Each slice has fragrant, chewy sticky rice around a mellow mung-bean and coconut filling, neatly wrapped in green banana leaves.
Bánh tét đậu xanh dừa chay

This Tay Ninh vegetarian sticky-rice cake wraps mung beans, coconut and sugar in glutinous rice and banana leaves for a gently sweet, nutty flavor. Bep Viet has adapted a family-sized loaf with clear steps for soaking, wrapping and steady simmering.
Let the cake cool slightly, then slice it with a clean knife for breakfast or a snack. Refrigerate leftovers and reheat thoroughly before eating.
One medium vegetarian sticky-rice cake, sliced into about 16 servings.
The rice needs soaking and the cake simmers for several hours; actual cooking time depends on the loaf's size.
Soak the rice and mung beans separately and drain them well before wrapping to prevent a soggy cake.
Wrap the cake firmly and tie it evenly. Add more boiling water if the pot level drops.
Use clean banana leaves and ties; cool promptly and refrigerate any leftovers.

names: Hanoi snail and green banana noodle soup
Ốc nấu chuối đậu ăn bún
fields: A hot bowl of rice vermicelli with tender snails, soft nutty green banana, seasoned tofu and a golden broth fragrant with fermented rice and perilla.
Ốc nấu chuối đậu ăn bún

Bún ốc chuối đậu gợi vị bùi của chuối xanh, ốc giòn, đậu phụ vàng và nước dùng chua dịu từ mẻ. Bếp Việt biên tập phần nước dùng vừa đủ cho gia đình, nấu chuối mềm nhưng giữ miếng và cho ốc vào sau để không dai.
Blanch the vermicelli and divide among bowls. Add the broth, snails, banana, tofu and pork, then garnish with perilla, lolot leaves and scallions. Serve hot.
Four bowls of snail noodle soup with green banana, tofu, pork belly and herbs.
Thời gian ngâm ốc tùy loại và nguồn; ốc cần được nấu chín hoàn toàn trước khi ăn.
Hanoi snail and green banana noodle soup
Soak live snails in clean water with a few chili slices or rice-rinsing water, rinse thoroughly, then boil completely before removing the meat.
Soak the green banana in salted water with a little vinegar to reduce browning and astringency.
Stir-fry the snails separately and return them to the pot only for the last few minutes to keep them tender-crisp.
A neat tapered cake with soft, chewy rice dough, well-seasoned pork, lightly crunchy wood ear mushrooms and a subtle banana-leaf aroma.

Bánh răng bừa Phụng Công có dáng thuôn dài như chiếc răng bừa, lớp bột gạo mềm ôm phần nhân thịt, hành và mộc nhĩ thơm. Bếp Việt biên tập cách làm bằng bột gạo xay sẵn, khuấy bột đến độ sánh rồi gói lá chuối và hấp chín.
Unwrap while warm and enjoy as is or with lightly seasoned fish sauce. These cakes are best freshly steamed.
Twelve tapered rice cakes filled with pork and wood ear mushrooms, three per person.
Bột cần nghỉ trước khi khuấy; hấp đến khi lớp bột trong đều từ giữa ra mép.
Stir the batter constantly over low heat until it is partially cooked, smooth and free of lumps.
Spread the dough evenly, place the filling in the center and seal both ends so the cake does not split during steaming.
Steam until the rice dough turns translucent and chewy; do not crowd the steamer.

names: Cá trắm kho niêu đất Hà Nam
fields: Glossy brown black carp with firm flesh, fragrant galangal and ginger, and a rich reduced sauce to serve with hot rice.
Cá trắm kho niêu đất Hà Nam

Cá kho Vũ Đại gắn với làng Đại Hoàng, nổi bật bởi cá trắm đen kho chậm trong niêu cùng riềng, gừng, hành và gia vị đồng quê. Bếp Việt biên tập phiên bản bếp nhà với lửa nhỏ và thời gian rút gọn hơn cách kho làng nghề, giữ miếng cá săn và thấm vị.
Carefully transfer the fish to a plate, spoon over a little braising liquid and serve with steamed rice, pickles or boiled greens.
Six portions of black carp slowly braised in a clay pot with galangal, ginger, pork belly and caramel sauce.
Đây là phiên bản bếp nhà rút gọn; cách kho làng nghề truyền thống thường lâu hơn đáng kể.
Line the bottom of the clay pot with galangal and arrange the fish in a single layer to reduce sticking.
Keep the heat low and steady; add boiling water around the edge of the pot as needed, and do not turn the fish while braising.
The traditional village method may take considerably longer; monitor tenderness and liquid levels throughout this home version.

names: Tay Ninh pomelo peel vegetarian rolls
fields: Rosy-orange vegetarian rolls with a light crunch from pomelo pith and papaya, fragrant toasted rice powder and a gentle tang with a hint of chili.

Nem bưởi Tây Ninh tận dụng cùi bưởi và đu đủ xanh để tạo viên nem chay có độ giòn sần, vị chua dịu và mùi thính rang. Bếp Việt biên tập mẻ nhỏ, khử vị đắng kỹ, nêm gia vị thực vật và hướng dẫn lên men ngắn trong dụng cụ sạch.
Unwrap and serve the rolls with Vietnamese coriander or young erythrina leaves and pepper salt. Refrigerate once they reach the desired tang.
Twelve small vegetarian pomelo-peel rolls, served with aromatic leaves and pepper salt.
Thời gian lên men phụ thuộc nhiệt độ và độ ráo nguyên liệu; giữ lạnh khi nem vừa chua dịu.
Tay Ninh pomelo peel vegetarian rolls
Boil and rinse the pomelo pith several times to reduce bitterness, then squeeze very dry.
Use clean utensils, dry wrapping leaves and fresh ingredients. Do not eat if the rolls smell unusual, feel slimy or show signs of spoilage.
Fermentation time varies with room temperature. Check after a few hours and refrigerate as soon as the rolls become mildly tangy.

names: Bánh pía sầu riêng trứng muối
fields: A fragrant golden pastry with delicate flaky layers and a rich mung bean and durian filling wrapped around a gently salty egg yolk.
Bánh pía sầu riêng trứng muối

Bánh pía Sóc Trăng nổi bật với lớp vỏ cán nhiều lớp và phần nhân đậu xanh sầu riêng, thường có lòng đỏ trứng muối ở giữa. Bếp Việt biên tập mẻ bánh gia đình theo kỹ thuật bột nước bọc bột dầu, cán cuộn nhiều lượt để tạo lớp vỏ xốp thơm.
Let the pastries cool completely and serve with hot tea. Store in an airtight container and observe a safe shelf life because the filling contains egg and moisture.
Eight medium pia pastries filled with mung bean and durian, each with a salted egg yolk.
Cần để bột nghỉ và cán cuộn nhiều lượt; thời gian nướng tùy lò và kích thước bánh.
Rest the dough between rolling stages so the layers do not shrink and are easier to coil.
Cook the filling until firm enough to roll into balls; a wet filling will prevent the pastry from separating into layers.
Bake in two stages and brush with egg yolk during the second stage for an even golden finish without burning.

names: Bánh mì que pate chí chương
fields: Golden crisp bread sticks with a soft crumb and fragrant pâté, dipped in gently spicy red chí chương.
Bánh mì que pate chí chương

Bánh mì que Hải Phòng giản dị với ổ bánh thon giòn, lớp pate gan béo thơm và chí chương cay nồng. Bếp Việt biên tập phiên bản tại nhà dùng pate đã chế biến sẵn từ nguồn tin cậy, làm nóng bánh sát lúc ăn để giữ lớp vỏ giòn.
Split the warm bread lengthwise, spread with pâté and toast once more. Serve chí chương separately so everyone can adjust the heat.
Eight small pâté-filled bread sticks served with mildly spicy chí chương.
Dùng pate chế biến sẵn để rút gọn thời gian; thời gian nướng tùy lò và độ dày ổ bánh.
Choose cooked, packaged pâté and follow its storage instructions; do not leave it at room temperature for long.
Toast the bread just before serving; adding pâté too early will soften the crust.
Chí chương is distinctly hot; add a little at a time, or use red chili sauce if it is unavailable.
Fluffy rice topped with fragrant clams, crisp fresh greens, nutty peanuts and crunchy pork cracklings, with clear hot clam broth on the side.

Cơm hến Huế phối hợp cơm nguội, hến nhỏ, rau thái mảnh, đậu phộng, tóp mỡ và mắm ruốc; nước luộc hến nóng thường được dùng kèm. Bếp Việt cân chỉnh thành phần cho mâm gia đình, giữ từng lớp nguyên liệu riêng để người ăn trộn theo khẩu vị.
Arrange the rice, herbs, clams, peanuts and pork cracklings in bowls. Serve with hot clam broth and diluted fermented shrimp paste; mix just before eating.
Four bowls of clam rice with herbs, peanuts, pork cracklings and fermented shrimp paste, served with hot clam broth.
Thời gian làm sạch hến tùy lượng cát và loại hến; luôn lọc nước luộc trước khi dùng.
Use clean clams, cook them completely and strain out all grit; bring the broth to a boil before keeping it hot for serving.
If cooking rice ahead, cool it quickly, refrigerate it and use it the same day; do not leave cooked rice at room temperature for long.
Fermented shrimp paste is salty and intense; dissolve it and add gradually so it does not overpower the clams.

names: Con Hen Island sweet corn pudding, Hue
fields: A golden bowl of sweet corn pudding with plump tender kernels, lightly thickened syrup and a little fragrant coconut cream.

Chè bắp Cồn Hến tận dụng vị ngọt thơm của bắp non, nấu cùng nước luộc lõi và đường thành món chè mềm dịu. Bếp Việt biên tập phiên bản gia đình ít ngọt, điểm một lớp nước cốt dừa mỏng để giữ vị ngô làm trung tâm.
Spoon into bowls and serve warm, or cool and chill. Add the coconut milk just before serving so the corn remains the main flavor.
Four bowls of gently sweet young-corn pudding, with coconut milk to taste.
Độ mềm phụ thuộc độ non của bắp; bắp già cần nấu lâu hơn và có thể ít ngọt hơn.
Con Hen Island sweet corn pudding, Hue
Choose young, milky corn and cut close to the cob while keeping the kernels whole and avoiding the tough core.
Stir gently after adding the tapioca starch so the kernels stay intact.
If using fresh coconut milk, heat it gently with a pinch of salt and use it the same day.

names: Bun thang (Hanoi chicken and egg noodle soup)
fields: A clear, delicate noodle soup with shredded chicken, omelet, Vietnamese pork sausage and fine radish strips, finished with fragrant Vietnamese coriander.
Bun thang (Hanoi chicken and egg noodle soup)

Bún thang Hà Nội được nhận ra bởi nước dùng gà trong, sợi bún nhỏ và nhiều phần nhân thái chỉ xếp gọn: gà, trứng, giò lụa, củ cải và rau thơm. Bếp Việt biên tập phiên bản gia đình, ninh nước dùng vừa thời gian và tách từng nguyên liệu để tô bún thanh, rõ vị.
Place the vermicelli in bowls and arrange the chicken, egg, pork sausage and radish in delicate clusters. Ladle over piping-hot broth and serve fermented shrimp paste separately to taste.
Four bowls of fine rice vermicelli with shredded chicken, thin omelet strips, Vietnamese pork sausage and clear chicken broth.
Khâu thái và bày topping cần tỉ mỉ; có thể nấu nước dùng trước và hoàn thiện tô ngay trước bữa ăn.
Skim frequently and simmer gently so the broth stays clear without a rolling boil.
Cook the egg in a thin omelet, cool it and cut it into even strips.
If using fermented shrimp paste or belostomatid oil, serve it separately and add a little at a time; both may be omitted.

names: Da Nang vermicelli with fermented anchovy sauce
Bún mắm thịt quay Đà Nẵng
fields: A colorful bowl layered with crisp greens, savory pork, nutty roasted peanuts and moderately spicy fermented anchovy sauce.
Bún mắm thịt quay Đà Nẵng

Bún mắm nêm Đà Nẵng có lớp mắm nêm thơm mạnh làm điểm nhấn, đi cùng bún tươi, thịt heo, chả, rau sống, đu đủ xanh và đậu phộng. Bếp Việt biên tập công thức trộn tại nhà, pha mắm nêm cùng thơm và chanh để cân bằng vị mặn, ngọt, chua, cay.
Arrange the vermicelli, greens, cucumber, papaya, pork and sausage in bowls. Add the separately mixed fermented anchovy sauce, sprinkle with peanuts and toss just before eating.
Four bowls of rice vermicelli tossed with fermented anchovy sauce, roast pork, sausage, fresh herbs, green papaya and peanuts.
Tô bún hoàn thiện nhanh; pha mắm nêm từ từ vì độ mặn và độ sệt thay đổi theo sản phẩm.
Da Nang vermicelli with fermented anchovy sauce
Fermented anchovy sauce is salty and pungent; start with a small amount, taste and add more as needed.
Buy freshly cooked roast pork from a trusted source or roast it at home; refrigerate any leftovers.
Dry the greens and cucumber thoroughly so the dressing does not become watery.
Soft, thin rice wrappers enclose a tender egg and are served with clear, aromatic broth, fried shallots and tangy pickled bamboo shoots.

A Lạng Sơn specialty of thin rice sheets wrapped around a softly cooked egg, served with hot pork-bone broth, minced pork and fried shallots. Bếp Việt adapts the steaming method to a lidded nonstick pan for home cooks.
Arrange the rolls on small plates and serve the hot broth alongside or spooned over to taste. Eat while the egg is still soft with pickled bamboo shoots and cilantro.
4 servings, each with hot egg rice rolls and a bowl of pork-bone broth.
Bếp Việt adapts the traditional cloth steamer to a lidded nonstick pan; adjust steaming time for wrapper thickness and preferred egg doneness.
rice rolls with hot bone broth
Keep the batter thin enough to spread; stir before each roll because rice flour settles.
Cover briefly so the white sets while the yolk stays soft; cook longer if you prefer a firm yolk.
Prepare and keep the broth hot, then cook the rolls just before serving so they do not dry out.
A dark-green soup fragrant with lemongrass, tender chicken and offal, and a clear bitter-leaf finish softened by a little fermented-rice tang.

A soup associated with Mường communities in the Thanh Hóa highlands, known for a gentle bitterness followed by a clean sweetness. Bếp Việt’s home version uses thoroughly cleaned chicken offal, chicken and a little fermented rice, with an option to reduce the leaves for first-time tasters.
Ladle into bowls while hot, dividing the meat and broth evenly. Serve as a soup with rice; offer extra chili or fermented rice on the side for a stronger flavour.
4 bowls, served hot as part of a family meal.
Preparation time depends on cleaning the chicken offal. Substitute chicken meat alone for a quicker, milder version.
bitter leaf soup with chicken offal
Buy edible bitter leaves from a trusted source; do not forage wild leaves unless you can identify them with certainty.
Clean the chicken offal thoroughly and cook it completely; use chicken meat alone for a milder soup.
Start with fewer leaves, taste and add more gradually; overcooking can make the leaves mushy and the bitterness harsh.

names: Hải Dương Field Perch Noodle Soup
Bún cá rô đồng xứ Đông
fields: White rice vermicelli in a light golden fish broth topped with golden perch, tomato, green water celery and fragrant herbs.
Bún cá rô đồng xứ Đông

A bowl from the former Hải Dương region pairs boiled and deboned field perch, lightly fried until golden, with fish-bone broth and greens such as water celery or mustard greens. Bếp Việt uses cleaned perch, carefully checks for bones and keeps the broth delicately seasoned.

Blanch the vermicelli and divide among bowls with quickly blanched water celery or greens. Add the fried fish, pour over hot broth and finish with scallions and dill. Serve promptly to keep the fish crisp.
4 hot bowls, each with field perch, greens and broth.
Prep time assumes the fish has been cleaned by the fishmonger. Allow extra time to clean it yourself and remove bones carefully.
Hải Dương Field Perch Noodle Soup
Buy properly cleaned perch from a trusted fishmonger and check carefully for bones; simmer the head and bones in a filter bag for the broth.
Fry the fish in a properly heated pan and turn gently so the pieces stay intact.
Do not overcook the greens; blanching separately keeps their colour bright and the broth clear.
Deep-green, flattened glutinous-rice cakes with a soft, chewy wrapper and a fragrant brown-sugar, sesame and peanut filling.

A Tày specialty from Lạng Sơn: chewy green glutinous-rice cakes coloured and scented with mugwort leaves, often filled with sugar, sesame and peanuts. Bếp Việt uses vegetable oil instead of animal fat, making this home version suitable for a vegetarian meal; the cakes are best eaten the day they are made.
Lightly brush the cakes with oil, arrange on clean banana leaves and serve while soft. They pair well with hot tea and need no dipping sauce.
12 small mugwort cakes with sesame-peanut filling, best eaten the same day.
This home adaptation uses thoroughly cooked mugwort and vegetable oil. Glutinous rice flour absorbs water differently, so add hot water gradually.
Choose tender mugwort leaves, wash well and cook until very soft before pounding or blending; do not use concentrated limewater.
Knead while the leaves are still warm, adding hot water a little at a time until the dough is pliable but not sticky.
Fresh cakes are best the same day. Wrap leftovers airtight, refrigerate and steam again before serving.

names: Sa Đéc Hu Tieu Noodle Soup
Hủ tiếu sợi gạo Sa Đéc
fields: A bowl of tender white rice noodles in a clear, gently sweet broth, topped with sliced pork, shrimp, bean sprouts and fresh garlic chives.
Hủ tiếu sợi gạo Sa Đéc

Sa Đéc hu tieu is known for smooth white rice noodles that stay tender without turning mushy, served in a light pork-bone broth. Bếp Việt’s home version uses dried shrimp for depth and tops the bowl with pork and fresh shrimp; traditional broth may be simmered longer.
Briefly blanch the hu tieu noodles and divide among bowls. Arrange the pork, shrimp, bean sprouts and chives on top, then ladle over piping-hot broth. Serve lime, chili and soy sauce on the side.
4 bowls of rice-noodle soup with pork, shrimp and a light broth.
This home version simmers the bones for about an hour to save time. Traditional stock may be cooked longer; adjust blanching to the noodles you use.
Sa Đéc Hu Tieu Noodle Soup
Use Sa Đéc rice noodles if available; follow the package directions and do not soak too long or they may turn mushy.
Simmer the bones gently and skim regularly for a clear, delicate broth.
Offer greens, lime, chili and soy sauce at the table; keep the broth light rather than overly sweet.
Evenly golden, fully cooked cakes scented with dill and tangerine zest, moist but not crumbly.

Chả rươi is a seasonal autumn dish from Vietnam’s northern delta, especially associated with Tứ Kỳ in Hải Dương. Ragworms are combined with minced pork, egg, dill, and a little tangerine zest for cakes that are aromatic, tender inside, and golden at the edges. Bếp Việt has edited the quantities for a home skillet, keeping the seasoning light so the ragworm flavor remains distinct.
Serve hot with steamed rice or vermicelli, fresh herbs, and a gently tart fish-sauce dip. Cut into portions after the cakes have rested for a few minutes.
Serves 4 as a savory dish with rice or vermicelli and fresh herbs.
Cooking time depends on cake thickness and stove heat; cut into one cake to verify the center is fully cooked.
Tứ Kỳ Hải Dương ragworm cakes
If using frozen ragworms, thaw them in the refrigerator, remove any debris, and discard any ingredient with an off smell.
Finely grate only a little of the colored tangerine peel to add aroma without bitterness.
Cook moderately thin cakes over medium heat so the center cooks through before the outside becomes too dark.

names: Tung Lò Mò Chăm Beef Sausage, An Giang
fields: Golden grilled tung lò mò with a juicy center, served with fresh herbs and cucumber.

Tung lò mò is a beef sausage associated with the Chăm community in An Giang, usually grilled until its casing turns fragrant and lightly browned. Bếp Việt’s home version uses a ready-made product, cooks it through, and serves it with fresh vegetables.
Cut the sausage diagonally after grilling and serve with fresh herbs, cucumber, and rice vermicelli or hot rice. Offer lime-pepper salt on the side.
Serves 4 with rice or vermicelli and fresh vegetables.
Heating time varies with the sausage diameter and whether it is raw or precooked; follow the package instructions.
Tung Lò Mò Chăm Beef Sausage, An Giang
Choose tung lò mò from a trusted seller and follow the package storage instructions.
Grill over medium heat and turn often so the casing does not burn before the center is hot.
If the product is raw, cook it completely according to the maker’s directions and keep it separate from raw food.

names: An Giang Sầu Đâu Salad with Dried Snakehead
Sầu Đâu Leaf and Dried Snakehead Salad
fields: Lightly bitter leaves and crisp papaya, savory dried snakehead, and a balanced sweet-sour tamarind dressing.
Sầu Đâu Leaf and Dried Snakehead Salad

This An Giang salad pairs the gentle bitterness of sầu đâu leaves with savory dried snakehead, boiled pork, and a sweet-tart tamarind fish-sauce dressing. Bếp Việt mixes it in small batches so the leaves stay fresh and the fish does not break apart.
Toss just before serving and finish with roasted peanuts and herbs. Serve with hot rice or as a starter.
Serves 4 as a shared salad or light starter.
Preparation time depends on the saltiness and dryness of the fish; soak it according to the seller’s directions if needed.
An Giang Sầu Đâu Salad with Dried Snakehead
Buy tender sầu đâu leaves from a trusted local source; blanch briefly and taste to manage bitterness.
Grill or pan-cook the dried fish until fragrant, then remove all bones before mixing.
Cool the dressing and add gradually; mix only the amount you plan to serve so the salad does not turn watery.

names: Cầu Mống Roast Veal, Quảng Nam
fields: Tender aromatic veal with a golden edge, rolled with herbs and rice paper and dipped in pineapple anchovy sauce.

Cầu Mống roast veal is known for tender slices with a fragrant golden edge, eaten with fresh herbs, rice paper, and anchovy sauce. Bếp Việt adapts the presentation and rolling style for a smaller oven-roasted cut at home.
Arrange the veal, herbs, green banana, starfruit, and rice paper in separate groups. Mix pineapple into the anchovy sauce and season with garlic and chili; roll each bite as you eat.
Serves 4; roll the veal with fresh herbs, rice paper, and anchovy sauce.
Roasting time varies with the shape and thickness of the cut; a reliable food thermometer is more accurate than timing alone.
Cầu Mống Roast Veal, Quảng Nam
Buy fresh veal from a inspected supplier, keep it chilled, and prevent raw meat from touching ready-to-eat vegetables.
Roast an evenly thick piece; use a food thermometer and let the meat rest before slicing.
Season anchovy sauce gradually because saltiness varies between products.

names: Mekong Delta Cá Lóc Nướng Trui
fields: Fragrant, fully cooked fish with flaky white flesh and lightly charred skin, served with herbs and tamarind fish sauce.

Cá lóc nướng trui is a rustic southern Vietnamese dish, traditionally cooked whole over straw to preserve the fish’s natural sweetness. Bếp Việt adds a home oven method; the fish is cleaned for convenience but its skin is kept intact.
Peel back the charred skin, lift the fish from the bones, and roll it with herbs, cucumber, starfruit, green banana, and rice paper. Serve tamarind fish sauce on the side.
Serves 4 as a shared grilled fish, rolled with rice paper and vegetables.
Whole fish cooks at different rates depending on size and the oven; check the thickest flesh near the backbone before serving.
Mekong Delta Cá Lóc Nướng Trui
For traditional outdoor roasting, leave the fish whole and scaled and use a safe, well-ventilated fire area.
For home cooking, ask the fish seller to clean the fish while leaving its skin on; roast until the flesh turns opaque and separates easily from the bones.
Keep raw fish and its juices away from ready-to-eat vegetables; use separate boards and tongs.
Glossy golden rice with tender, separate grains; sweet shredded chicken with Vietnamese coriander and shallots, balanced by pickles and garlic-chili fish sauce.

Tam Ky chicken rice pairs golden, fragrant rice cooked in chicken stock with boiled free-range chicken shredded and tossed with shallots and Vietnamese coriander. Bep Viet has edited a family-size version that keeps the Tam Ky style distinct: the chicken is boiled once, the rice is cooked separately in stock, and the plate is served with pickles and garlic fish sauce rather than being relabeled as Hoi An chicken rice.

Plate the hot rice separately and arrange the chicken tossed with Vietnamese coriander alongside it. Serve with sweet-and-sour pickled papaya, fresh greens and garlic-chili fish sauce; a small bowl of hot chicken broth is optional.
Four portions of golden rice cooked in chicken stock, served with shredded chicken, Vietnamese coriander and pickles.
Boiling time varies with the chicken's size; use a food thermometer to confirm it is safely cooked.
shredded chicken with Vietnamese coriander and rice
Cook the chicken through; the thickest part of the thigh should reach at least 74°C. Let it rest before shredding.
Lightly toast the rice with a little chicken fat and turmeric before cooking so the grains are fragrant, fluffy and evenly colored.
Toss the chicken with Vietnamese coriander, shallots and fish sauce just before serving to keep it from becoming watery.
Lightly glossy rice noodles with tender char siu, crisp sweet potato and nutty peanuts; the sweet-sour sauce coats the dish lightly while fresh herbs brighten it.

Lang Son sour pho is a dry noodle dish of soft rice noodles, char siu pork, crisp fried sweet potato, roasted peanuts and fresh herbs. A measured sweet-and-sour dressing seasons the ingredients while keeping their textures distinct. Bep Viet has adapted it for a family kitchen, using pan-seared pork shoulder and an easy-to-adjust sauce.

Divide the rice noodles among shallow bowls and arrange the pork, fried sweet potato, cucumber, herbs and peanuts on top. Add the sauce gradually, toss gently and serve at once to keep the potato crisp.
Four plates of sweet-and-sour pho salad with char siu pork, crisp sweet potato, peanuts and fresh herbs.
The time excludes soaking the sweet potato; adjust the dressing to your family's preferred sweet-sour balance.
sour pho with crisp sweet potato
Soak the cut sweet potato in lightly salted cold water, then dry it thoroughly before frying to prevent discoloration and help it crisp.
Cook the dressing until lightly thickened. Taste for sweet, sour and salty balance before serving, since vinegar and calamansi vary in acidity.
Toss the noodles with the dressing just before eating and avoid adding too much, which can make the dish soggy.

names: Phu Ly Rice Rolls with Grilled Pork
Ha Nam Rice Rolls with Grilled Pork
fields: Soft, thin rice sheets wrap pork and wood ear mushroom filling, finished with golden fried shallots; charred grilled pork and balanced dipping sauce complete the meal.
Phu Ly Rice Rolls with Grilled Pork
Ha Nam Rice Rolls with Grilled Pork

Phu Ly steamed rice rolls are known for soft, lightly chewy rice sheets, fragrant fried shallots, a generous bowl of seasoned fish sauce and grilled pork on the side. Bep Viet has adapted the dish for a home kitchen using a nonstick pan instead of a traditional steaming cloth, while keeping the hot rolls and grilled-pork pairing associated with Phu Ly.
Serve the hot rice rolls on a plate with fried shallots and grilled pork. Pour warm fish sauce into a small bowl and add herbs and chili to taste.
Four servings of hot rice rolls with pork filling, grilled pork patties, fried shallots and fish sauce.
Cooking time depends on the pan size; maintain steady heat and keep each sheet thin.
steamed rice rolls with grilled pork
Rest the batter for about 20 minutes and stir before each sheet so it stays smooth and does not settle.
Brush the nonstick pan with a very thin film of oil, cook each sheet over medium heat and briefly cover so it cooks evenly without drying.
Grill the pork patties until fully cooked and browned at the edges; do not press them too hard or they may dry out.

names: O Thum Chicken Roasted with Kaffir Lime Leaves
Tri Ton Chicken Roasted with Kaffir Lime Leaves
fields: Golden chicken fragrant with kaffir lime leaves and lemongrass, lightly crisp on the outside and moist within, served with tangy chili-lime salt.
Tri Ton Chicken Roasted with Kaffir Lime Leaves

O Thum chicken roasted with kaffir lime leaves is associated with the Seven Mountains area of An Giang and local Khmer cooking. The chicken is marinated with lemongrass, garlic, chili and fragrant kaffir lime leaves, then cooked over a bed of lemongrass and leaves until the skin is golden and the meat tender. Bep Viet has adapted the method for a lidded cast-iron pot that is easier to use and monitor at home.

Cut the chicken into serving pieces and sprinkle with shredded kaffir lime leaves. Serve hot with cabbage and Vietnamese coriander salad, cucumber and kaffir-lime salt while the skin is still fragrant.
One chicken weighing about 1.5 kg, cooked with lemongrass, garlic and kaffir lime leaves, served with fresh greens and dipping sauce.
Local descriptions give a cooking time of about 40 minutes; for a home pot, adjust for the chicken size and verify a safe internal temperature.
An Giang chicken roasted with kaffir lime leaves
O Thum roasted chicken from Tri Ton
O Thum Chicken Roasted with Kaffir Lime Leaves
Use fresh chicken weighing about 1.3–1.6 kg so it cooks evenly in a home pot; do not cook a chicken that is still frozen inside.
Keep the pot covered and line the bottom with lemongrass to prevent scorching; check that the thigh reaches at least 74°C before serving.
Kaffir lime leaves have a stronger aroma than regular lime leaves. If unavailable, substitute lime zest and lime leaves, though the flavor will differ from the local original.

names: A bowl of Quang Ngai don soup
ingredients: Fresh live don clams in the shell
fields: A clear broth with gentle river-shellfish sweetness, tender don meat, fragrant scallions and chili, and toasted rice cracker for a crisp, nutty finish.
A bowl of Quang Ngai don soup

Don is a brackish-water shellfish associated with the Tra and Ve rivers in Quang Ngai. The dish highlights the shellfish's natural sweetness in a delicate broth, accented with scallions, herbs and chili; toasted rice cracker is often broken into the bowl at the table. Bep Viet has adapted the local serving style for a family meal, with careful straining to remove grit and thorough cooking.
Ladle the don and hot broth into bowls, then garnish with scallions, cilantro, pepper and green chili. Break the toasted rice cracker into bite-size pieces and add to the bowl or serve on the side.
Four bowls of don soup in a clear shellfish broth, served with toasted rice crackers, scallions and green chili.
Soaking and purging time is not included; simmering time depends on the clams' size and freshness.
don soup served with toasted rice crackers
Choose live don clams from a traceable source; soak them and change the water several times to release sand before cooking.
After removing the meat, strain the cooking liquid through a fine sieve or clean cloth to remove any remaining grit.
Break the rice cracker into the bowl just before eating to retain some crispness; season with fish sauce and chili to taste.
Fresh live don clams in the shell

names: Tuyen Quang Tay cone-shaped sticky rice cake
Bánh sừng bò của người Tày
fields: Neat cone-shaped cakes have tender, glossy sticky rice around nutty black beans, with a gentle leaf aroma; serve warm with sesame salt.
Bánh sừng bò của người Tày
