A traditional Tay cone-shaped sticky rice cake wrapped in green leaves with black beans. Bếp Việt adapts the soaking, wrapping and simmering method for a small home batch so the rice cooks tender and fragrant.
Let the cakes drain briefly, then unwrap while warm. Serve with sesame salt or lightly crushed peanut salt.
6 cone-shaped sticky rice cakes with black beans, served with sesame salt.
Boiling time depends on cake size and rice variety; test one cake before turning off the heat.
Tuyen Quang Tay sticky rice cake
cone-shaped sticky rice with black beans
Tuyen Quang Tay cone-shaped sticky rice cake
Soak the sticky rice and black beans separately so they soften evenly before wrapping.
Tie the leaves firmly enough to hold their shape while leaving room for the rice to expand.
Keep the cakes covered with water at a gentle boil; larger cakes may need extra time.

ingredients: Young mustard greens, lettuce and herbs
fields: Palm-sized golden cá linh fritters with a delicate crisp coating and tender, fragrant fish, served with fresh greens and sweet-sour fish sauce.
A Mekong Delta seasonal fish dish: small cá linh are coated in a light egg batter and fried golden. Bếp Việt adapts the home method and pairs the crisp fish with fresh garden greens.
Serve immediately while crisp. Wrap with young mustard greens, lettuce and herbs, then dip in sweet-sour fish sauce.
4 portions of crisp battered fish with fresh greens and sweet-sour fish sauce.
Small fish cook quickly; frying time varies with fish size and oil temperature. Make sure the fish is cooked through.
Choose fresh small fish, rinse gently and dry thoroughly so the batter adheres evenly.
Use just enough batter to coat the fish; the mixture should not be runny.
Fry in small batches at moderate heat and drain on a rack to preserve crispness.
Young mustard greens, lettuce and herbs

names: Mixed garden greens soup with shrimp
fields: A gently sweet shrimp broth with tender green leaves and pink shrimp, served hot and fresh.

A light Vietnamese home-style soup combining seasonal garden greens with fresh shrimp for a gently sweet, clear broth. Bếp Việt adapts the order of adding greens so each variety stays tender and green.
Ladle into bowls and serve hot with steamed rice and a mild savory dish. Eat promptly so the greens keep their color and freshness.
4 bowls of seasonal garden greens soup with fresh shrimp.
Add the greens to a briskly boiling broth and cook for no more than 3 minutes in total to preserve their color.
Mixed garden greens soup with shrimp
Combine three to five tender leafy greens; trim tough parts and wash thoroughly.
Pound or chop the shrimp coarsely so the broth is flavorful while small shrimp pieces remain.
Add firmer greens first and tender leaves last; cook only until just done.

names: Ben Tre hand-cut rice noodle and duck soup
fields: Soft, lightly chewy rice noodles sit in fragrant ginger duck broth with tender meat; serve with a small dish of ginger fish sauce.

A rustic Ben Tre noodle soup made by rolling rice dough and cutting the strands directly into a simmering duck broth. Bếp Việt adapts the home method for tender noodles, a gently cloudy broth and fragrant ginger.
Ladle noodles and broth into bowls, top with duck, scallions, herbs and pepper. Serve ginger fish sauce on the side for dipping the meat.
5 bowls of hand-cut rice noodles with tender duck in ginger broth.
Flour absorbs water differently; adjust the dough until pliable, not wet. Cut strands into gently simmering broth.
Ben Tre banh canh bot xat
Ben Tre hand-cut rice noodle and duck soup
Knead until the dough is smooth, pliable and no longer sticky; add water gradually.
Roll and cut the noodles directly over gently simmering broth to prevent them sticking together.
After adding the dough, avoid a hard boil because starch can settle on the bottom of the pot.
Loose golden turmeric noodles with fully cooked pork offal, scallions and aromatic Vietnamese coriander.

A humble Hue noodle dish combining rice vermicelli with golden turmeric, thoroughly cleaned pork offal, onion and Vietnamese coriander. Bếp Việt adapts the preparation to cook the offal fully and stir-fry the noodles briefly so they stay separate.
Serve hot with Vietnamese coriander, scallions and pepper. Add fresh chilli and a squeeze of lime to taste.
4 portions of turmeric rice vermicelli stir-fried with pork offal and herbs.
Boiling time depends on the type and size of offal; always cook it fully before stir-frying.
Clean and boil the offal until fully cooked; do not serve it raw or undercooked.
If using dried vermicelli, soak and blanch according to the package, then drain before stir-frying.
Cook the turmeric over medium heat and toss the noodles briefly so they do not break apart.

names: Hanoi Chả Cốm (Young Rice Pork Patties)
fields: Lightly golden patties with fragrant young rice flakes and a moist, tender center; serve hot with rice, noodles or herbs.

Pork and Vietnamese pork paste are mixed with fragrant young rice flakes, shaped into patties, briefly steamed and fried until lightly golden. This Bếp Việt home adaptation keeps the rice tender and aromatic.
Serve the patties hot with steamed rice, vermicelli or fresh herbs. Pickled vegetables help balance the richness.
Fry in small batches; timing depends on patty thickness.
Hanoi Chả Cốm (Young Rice Pork Patties)
If using dried rice flakes, soften with a little warm water first.
Brief steaming helps the patties hold their shape; fry over medium heat until the pork is cooked through.
Too much egg can make the mixture loose.

names: Quảng-Style Steamed Scad with Rice-Paper Rolls
fields: Just-cooked sweet fish wrapped with crisp greens and flexible rice paper, served with tangy garlic-chili sauce.

Small scad are steamed with scallion, lemongrass and chili, then wrapped with cassava rice paper, tender water spinach and herbs. A little filtered steaming liquid can enrich the dipping sauce in this central-coast meal.
Serve the hot fish with rice paper, greens and garlic-chili fish sauce. Wrap with herbs; add toasted rice crackers for crunch if desired.
4 servings of steamed fish with wrapping greens, rice paper and dipping sauce.
The 12–15 minute guide suits small fish; larger fish need longer until cooked through.
Quảng-Style Steamed Scad with Rice-Paper Rolls
Choose small, firm fish with clear eyes; clean and dry thoroughly.
Avoid over-steaming; timing depends on fish size and the steamer.
Strain any steaming liquid used in the dip and season gradually.
A lightly thickened coconut broth with naturally sweet vegetables; the roots, pumpkin and tofu stay tender but hold their shape.

A Southern Vietnamese noodle dish with root vegetables, pumpkin, just-ripe plantain, tofu and bean-curd sheets in vegetable broth enriched with coconut milk. This Bếp Việt version is served as a light soup with rice vermicelli.
Divide noodles among bowls and ladle over vegetables and broth. Top with peanuts and herbs; serve hot.
4 bowls of bún kiểm with vegetables in coconut broth.
Root-vegetable timing depends on size; cut evenly so pieces soften without breaking apart.
Soak bean-curd sheets and mushrooms until soft, then drain well.
Add pumpkin and plantain after firmer roots so the vegetables keep their shape.
Keep the heat low after adding coconut milk and avoid a vigorous boil.

names: Vietnamese Beef Hotpot with Coconut Vinegar (Bò Nhúng Giấm)
fields: A fragrant pineapple and lemongrass broth, gently sweet and sour; wrap just-cooked beef with herbs and noodles, then dip in mắm nêm.

Thin beef is dipped in coconut water broth with rice vinegar, lemongrass, onion and pineapple, then wrapped with vermicelli and vegetables in rice paper and served with mắm nêm. Its bright sweet-sour broth makes a convivial meal.
Keep the broth at a gentle simmer. Dip beef until cooked, wrap with vermicelli and vegetables in rice paper, and serve with pineapple mắm nêm.
4 shared servings with dipping broth, beef, noodles, greens and rice paper.
Prep time excludes eating at the table; keep the broth gently simmering so the beef stays tender.
Vietnamese Beef Hotpot with Coconut Vinegar (Bò Nhúng Giấm)
Slice beef across the grain and keep it chilled until serving.
Add vinegar gradually so the broth is bright rather than harsh.
Use separate utensils for raw and cooked meat; do not leave raw meat at room temperature.

names: Vietnamese Vegetarian Nem Thính (Mushroom and Toasted Rice Salad)
fields: Springy mushroom strands coated in nutty toasted rice powder, with soft glass noodles and fragrant lime leaf; wrap in greens or serve with vermicelli.

King oyster mushrooms are cut into strands, blanched and fried until springy, then tossed with glass noodles, toasted rice powder and lime leaves. This Bếp Việt version uses vegetarian seasoning and a plant-based dip with fresh greens.
Serve with wild fig leaves, perilla, lettuce, rice paper and vermicelli, alongside sweet-sour vegetarian dipping sauce or diluted soy sauce.
4 servings to wrap with greens or enjoy with noodles and rice paper.
Rice powder absorbs moisture quickly; add gradually just before serving to keep the mixture loose.
Vietnamese Vegetarian Nem Thính (Mushroom and Toasted Rice Salad)
Squeeze mushrooms dry after blanching to reduce oil splatter and help the rice powder coat evenly.
Cool mushrooms slightly before adding the powder so the mixture does not become damp and clumpy.
For a fully vegetarian meal, check seasonings, dipping sauce and rice paper for animal ingredients.
The rice cake is smooth and chewy, cut into neat pieces with peanuts evenly distributed throughout. It tastes gently of rice and peanuts, with a subtle note from nuoc nang.

Lang Dong peanut rice cake is ivory-white, soft and chewy, with roasted peanuts and the gentle alkaline note of nuoc nang. Bep Viet adapts the stirring method for rice flour at home and recommends only food-grade nuoc nang; do not make an ash solution yourself.
Let the rice cake cool slightly, then cut it into bite-size pieces. Serve with fermented soybean dip; add fresh herbs if desired.
Four servings of sliced rice cake with fermented soybean dipping sauce.
About 1 hour 30 minutes, not including the time for the rice cake to cool completely.
rice cake made with nuoc nang
Stir the powder in cold water before turning on the stove to limit clumping.
Only use water of food origin; Do not use self-filtered ash water or unlabeled chemicals.
Stir continuously over low heat until the dough is clear and the membrane is stretched; The cake will thicken as it cools.

names: Nam Dinh Festival Mung Bean Cake
fields: A golden, smooth mung bean sweet with a pleasantly firm, chewy texture, fragrant with ginger and finished with toasted sesame.
Nam Dinh Festival Mung Bean Cake

Nam Dinh che kho is a thick mung bean sweet, molded and served for festivals and holidays. Despite the word che, it is closer to a soft cake than a liquid dessert. Bep Viet keeps the mung bean, ginger and toasted sesame notes while moderating the sugar for a home-sized batch.
Let the mung bean sweet cool in the mold, then cut it into small pieces. Serve with hot tea after a meal or include it on a festival offering tray.
Six servings of thick mung bean che kho, molded and topped with toasted sesame.
About 4 hours 10 minutes, including soaking time; the beans can be soaked overnight.
Soak the mung beans until plump and steam them fully so the finished paste is smooth rather than grainy.
Cook over low heat, stirring continuously and scraping the pan so the mung bean paste does not scorch.
You can reduce the sugar slightly, but cook the paste until thick enough to hold its shape when cool.
Rau thơm và phần ăn kèm
The amber-brown broth balances savory and sweet notes; tofu is tender and well-seasoned, while the vegetables stay intact and the mushrooms remain juicy.

Mekong-style vegetarian mam kho simmers vegetables, mushrooms and tofu in a savory plant-based broth fragrant with lemongrass and lightly enriched with coconut milk. Bep Viet's fully plant-based version is a spoonable stew for rice, distinct from thick vegetarian kho quet dipping sauce.
Spoon the braising broth and vegetables into a warm serving bowl. Serve with steamed rice or fresh vermicelli, with fresh greens, chili and lime on the side.
Four servings of vegetables, mushrooms and tofu braised in a savory broth, served with rice or vermicelli.
About 55 minutes; prepare the vegetables ahead to shorten active cooking time.
Choose a fully plant-based fermented seasoning and check the label to make sure it contains no fish.
Lightly fry the tofu first to firm its surface, then braise it; handle gently to keep the pieces intact.
Add the vegetables that need longer cooking first, then the tofu and coconut milk. Taste before adding salt.
Rau thơm và phần ăn kèm

names: Mai Xa Chat Chat Clam Vermicelli
Quang Tri Chat Chat Clam Vermicelli
ingredients: Live chat chat clams in the shell
fields: A bowl of vermicelli topped with sweet, savory chat chat clams, toasted peanuts, crisp greens and warming ginger, with a mild soy-and-chili dressing.
Mai Xa Chat Chat Clam Vermicelli
Quang Tri Chat Chat Clam Vermicelli

Mai Xa bun hen is known for brackish-water chat chat, a small mollusk related to clams. Bep Viet adapts it as mixed vermicelli with soy sauce, chili sauce, herbs and peanuts, with a little cooking broth on the side; it does not use the fermented shrimp paste and taro stems found in some Hue bun hen versions.
Divide the rice vermicelli among bowls, then top with chat chat clams, herbs and peanuts. Break the rice cracker over each bowl. Serve soy-chili sauce and hot clam broth separately.
Four bowls of Mai Xa mixed vermicelli with chat chat clams, hot broth, greens, peanuts and toasted rice cracker.
About 1 hour 25 minutes, including soaking time for clams in their shells.
Use cleaned chat chat clams from a reputable seller. If buying them in their shells, soak them and change the water to release sand.
Avoid boiling the clams after their shells have just opened, or the meat may turn tough.
Serve the soy sauce and chili sauce separately so the clams' natural sweetness remains prominent.
Live chat chat clams in the shell
Rau thơm và phần ăn kèm

names: Phu Quoc Tram Mushroom and Shrimp Soup
fields: The clear broth is gently sweet from shrimp; tram mushrooms hold their shape and lend a characteristic mild bitterness, finished with scallions and cilantro.
Phu Quoc Tram Mushroom and Shrimp Soup

Phu Quoc tram mushroom soup evokes the forest mushroom season after the rains, with a gentle initial bitterness and a sweet finish. Bep Viet adapts it with shrimp for a light broth and uses safely prepared mushrooms. Phu Quoc is now part of An Giang Province, while the familiar dish name retains its local identity.
Ladle the hot soup into bowls and finish with scallions, cilantro and a little pepper. Serve with steamed rice and enjoy the mushrooms' gentle bitterness and sweet finish.
Four bowls of tram mushroom and shrimp soup, served hot with rice.
About 45 minutes when using cleaned mushrooms; prep time depends on the type of mushroom.
Use only tram mushrooms identified and prepared by a trusted supplier. Do not forage wild mushrooms without expert knowledge.
Blanch fresh mushrooms as directed by the seller and rinse before cooking. Thaw pre-cleaned frozen mushrooms in the refrigerator.
Add the mushrooms near the end and cook just until tender; prolonged cooking can make the broth more bitter.
Rau thơm và phần ăn kèm
Soft, distinct green rice grains with a gentle lotus-leaf aroma, complemented by nutty beans, lotus seeds and mildly sweet coconut.

Fragrant green young rice is steamed until just tender, then folded with fluffy mung beans, lotus seeds and lightly sweetened coconut. This Bếp Việt home adaptation keeps the grains soft without oversteaming.
Serve warm or slightly cooled, wrapped in a clean lotus leaf or arranged on a small plate. Reduce the sugar to emphasize the rice aroma.
Mung-bean soaking is passive time; steam the rice briefly to preserve its aroma and texture.
young rice with lotus seeds and mung beans
Fresh young rice is usually moist enough; add only a little water if it seems dry.
Steam for about 4–5 minutes, just until warm and tender; longer steaming can make the rice mushy and dull its aroma.
Drain the mung beans well before mashing so they stay fluffy.
Small lightly charred rolls with a soft, chewy rice wrapper and a moist, savory shrimp-and-pork filling; serve with herbs, pickles and dipping sauce.

Fresh shrimp is coarsely pounded and mixed with pork belly, shallot and cut rice noodles, then wrapped in fresh rice sheets and grilled until fragrant and lightly browned. This Bếp Việt home adaptation uses a grill pan or charcoal grill.
Serve hot with fresh herbs, green papaya pickles and sweet-and-sour fish sauce. Grill over charcoal or in a heavy pan.
4 servings, about 3–4 small rolls per person.
Grill in batches over medium heat so the wrappers do not burn before the filling is cooked.
Pound the shrimp in a mortar for a coarse texture; do not blend it into a paste.
Roll snugly so the rice sheet holds the filling without tearing; lightly moisten dry edges.
Grill over medium heat, turning evenly, and cook the shrimp and pork filling through before serving.

names: Phù Mỹ Freshwater Crab Noodle Soup
fields: A hot, fragrant crab broth with naturally set crab meat and roe, served over soft rice vermicelli and balanced with lime, chili and optional herbs.

Fresh field crabs are cleaned, pounded and strained, then gently simmered until their meat and roe set into the rustic broth of Phù Mỹ. This Bếp Việt home adaptation keeps the broth focused on crab and serves herbs on the side according to preference.
Divide the vermicelli into bowls and ladle over gently simmering crab broth. Serve toasted rice crackers, lime, chili and herbs separately; roasted peanuts are optional.
4 bowls, each with about 200 g rice vermicelli and hot crab broth.
Cleaning and pounding the crabs take most of the preparation time; simmer gently to keep the broth clear.
Phù Mỹ Freshwater Crab Noodle Soup
Wash the crabs thoroughly and strain through a fine sieve to remove sand and shell fragments.
Once the broth starts to simmer, avoid vigorous stirring so the crab meat can set.
Cook the crab thoroughly. Sea crab is not a direct substitute because it has a different flavor.

names: Bắc Kạn Tày-Style Bò Khai Greens with Egg
Tày-style stir-fried bò khai with egg
fields: Vivid green, tender-crisp shoots coated with fully cooked egg and fragrant garlic, served hot with steamed rice.
Tày-style stir-fried bò khai with egg

Tender bò khai shoots are snapped into short lengths, quickly stir-fried with garlic and tossed with egg until just cooked. This rustic dish is associated with Tày meals in Bắc Kạn; this Bếp Việt adaptation uses family-sized portions and keeps the greens vivid.
Transfer to a plate as soon as the egg is cooked and serve hot with steamed rice. Add a little chili if desired.
4 rice-meal servings, about 100 g raw bò khai greens per serving.
Drain the greens thoroughly after washing so they stir-fry instead of steaming in the pan.
Bắc Kạn Tày-Style Bò Khai Greens with Egg
Choose young tips, remove tough stems and damaged leaves, then wash and drain thoroughly.
Stir-fry quickly over high heat to preserve the green color and avoid excess liquid.
Cook the egg through; toss just enough for it to coat the greens without becoming dry.

names: Hòa Bình Buffalo Stew with Lá Lồm
fields: Tender, savory buffalo with the gentle sourness of lá lồm and a lightly thickened broth from broken rice, fragrant with ginger and garlic.

Buffalo is cleaned, lightly seared and slowly simmered with pounded lá lồm leaves and broken rice until the broth thickens slightly. This traditional Mường dish from Hòa Bình has a gentle sourness from the leaves; this Bếp Việt home adaptation uses a regular pot.
Ladle hot into deep bowls and serve as a hearty soup in a rice meal. Adjust the salt and sourness after the leaves have softened.
4 bowls served with rice, about 150 g raw buffalo per serving.
Simmering time depends on the toughness of the buffalo cut. If the liquid reduces before the meat is tender, add a little boiling water.
Hòa Bình buffalo lá lồm stew
Hòa Bình Buffalo Stew with Lá Lồm
If the buffalo has a strong aroma, rub it with ginger and rinse before cooking; searing or charring adds fragrance.
Lá lồm is naturally sour; add it gradually to avoid making the stew too tart.
Simmer gently until tender. If using a pressure cooker, follow its timing instructions and release pressure safely before opening.

names: Phú Thọ Sour Cassava-Leaf and Pork Rib Soup
fields: Tender ribs and soft cassava leaves in a gently sour, savory broth with fragrant shallot.

Fermented cassava leaves simmer with pork ribs for a gently sour, earthy soup associated with Phú Thọ home cooking. This Bếp Việt home adaptation keeps the seasoning light so the leaves and rib broth remain distinct.
Ladle into bowls and serve hot with steamed rice and a lightly seasoned main dish. Taste only after the leaves soften, since preserved leaves may already be salty.
4 shared bowls for a family meal.
Simmering time varies by rib cut; cook the cassava leaves until tender while keeping their strands intact.
pork rib and fermented cassava leaves
Phú Thọ Sour Cassava-Leaf and Pork Rib Soup
Use properly prepared, fermented cassava leaves; never use raw leaves.
Squeeze out some brine and taste before rinsing so the leaves do not become bland.
Season with salt or fish sauce at the end because preserved leaves can already be salty.

names: Trà Vinh Cháo Ám Snakehead Fish Porridge
fields: A gently thick porridge fragrant with fish and dried seafood, with tender snakehead, soft fish roe and crisp fresh greens.

Snakehead fish cooking broth becomes the base for rice porridge, enriched with boneless fish, dried shrimp and toasted dried squid. The Trà Vinh-style bowl is served with fresh greens, peanuts and a savory chili bean dip.

Ladle the hot porridge into bowls and top with fish, scallion and cilantro. Serve with blanched bean sprouts, bitter greens, shredded banana blossom, sesame rice crackers and a bean-sauce dip seasoned with fermented fish sauce, lime and chili to taste.
4 bowls of snakehead fish porridge, served hot with fresh greens and dipping sauce.
Cooking time depends on the rice; stir the bottom of the pot regularly to prevent sticking.
Trà Vinh Cháo Ám Snakehead Fish Porridge
Strain the fish broth before cooking the rice to remove small bones.
Flake the fish while warm and check carefully for remaining bones.
If fish roe is unavailable, omit it; chicken egg would change the dish’s character.

names: Cà Mau Stir-Fried Bồn Bồn with Dried Shrimp
fields: Ivory-white, crisp bồn bồn shoots coated with savory dried shrimp and fragrant shallot, without excess liquid.

Tender bồn bồn shoots stay crisp and sweet when quickly stir-fried over high heat with dried shrimp and shallot. This simple vegetable dish is associated with Cà Mau; the Bếp Việt adaptation keeps the sauce light so the vegetable remains the focus.
Serve as soon as the stir-fry is done, finished with black pepper and steamed rice. Add a little lime if you prefer a brighter flavor.
4 portions of lightly crisp stir-fried vegetables to serve with rice.
Total time excludes soaking the dried shrimp; stir-fry the shoots briefly to retain their crunch.
stir-fried cattail shoots with dried shrimp
Cà Mau Stir-Fried Bồn Bồn with Dried Shrimp
Use tender inner bồn bồn shoots and trim any tough ends; soak briefly in light salt water.
Drain thoroughly before stir-frying so the shoots do not steam and soften.
Cook quickly over high heat without covering the pan.

names: Huế Tapioca Dumpling and Roasted Pork Sweet Soup
fields: Soft, chewy, slightly translucent dumplings with a savory-sweet roasted pork center in fragrant ginger syrup that is not overly sweet.

Chewy, translucent tapioca dumplings enclose pork roasted and gently candied with rock sugar, then simmer in a light ginger syrup. This Bếp Việt home adaptation moderates the sweetness so the savory, rich filling remains clear, reflecting Huế’s distinctive sweet-and-savory dessert.
Spoon a few dumplings and ginger syrup into small bowls and finish with roasted peanuts. Serve warm for the ginger aroma or over ice for a cool dessert.
6 small bowls, served warm or chilled.
Total time varies with the water temperature and amount used to knead the dough; this recipe starts with cooked roast pork.
Huế tapioca dumplings with roasted pork
sweet soup with savory pork filling
Huế Tapioca Dumpling and Roasted Pork Sweet Soup
Dice the roast pork finely and trim away any overly tough skin so the filling is easy to wrap.
Knead the tapioca starch with hot water gradually, stopping when the dough is pliable and no longer sticky.
Once the dumplings float, simmer them for a few more minutes so the dough cooks evenly around the filling.

names: Hmong Mèn Mén from former Hà Giang
fields: Soft, fluffy grains of steamed corn with a naturally nutty aroma and no added seasoning.

Mèn mén is a traditional steamed corn dish of the Hmong people on the Đồng Văn Karst Plateau in former Hà Giang, now part of Tuyên Quang. Finely milled field corn is moistened, loosened and steamed twice, with the mixture fluffed between rounds so it cooks evenly. This Bếp Việt home version uses ready-ground cornmeal.
Serve hot with vegetable or bean soup; a separately served braise can accompany it for a non-vegetarian meal. The mèn mén itself keeps the natural flavor of corn.
4 portions of steamed ground field corn, served as the meal’s staple.
Traditional preparation can take 2–3 hours; this estimate assumes the corn is already milled and varies with grind size.
Hmong mèn mén from former Hà Giang province
Hmong Mèn Mén from former Hà Giang
Use finely milled field corn and sift out any hard hull pieces; do not use precooked instant polenta.
Sprinkle water in gradually and rub the meal until loose like damp sand, avoiding large clumps.
Steam twice and fluff the grains between rounds; water and timing depend on the grind and maturity of the corn.

names: Nộm sứa đỏ chấm mắm tôm
fields: Sứa giòn trong, đậu phụ vàng thơm, cùi dừa ngọt nhẹ; rau giữ độ tươi và nước chấm chua mặn vừa miệng.
Nộm sứa đỏ chấm mắm tôm

Nộm sứa đỏ Hải Phòng nổi bật với miếng sứa đỏ hồng trong giòn, ăn cùng đậu phụ nướng nghệ, cùi dừa, rau thơm và chén mắm tôm hoặc giấm bỗng. Bếp Việt biên tập công thức theo hướng gia đình, dùng sứa đã sơ chế và đóng gói an toàn; không tự xử lý sứa tươi chưa qua chế biến.
Xếp sứa và đồ ăn kèm riêng trên đĩa. Cuốn mỗi phần với lá tía tô, kinh giới hoặc lá sung, chấm mắm tôm pha giấm bỗng; dọn ngay sau khi trộn.
4 phần nộm sứa đỏ cuốn cùng rau thơm, cùi dừa, đậu phụ nướng và bánh tráng.
Khoảng 40 phút nếu dùng sứa đã sơ chế; thời gian có thể thay đổi theo hướng dẫn trên bao bì.
Chỉ mua sứa đỏ đã được sơ chế đúng quy trình từ cơ sở đáng tin cậy; không dùng sứa tươi tự đánh bắt.
Để sứa thật ráo trước khi bày để món không ra nước.
Nướng đậu phụ vừa vàng mặt, giữ bên trong mềm; pha nước chấm riêng để ai cũng gia giảm được.
Rau thơm và phần ăn kèm

names: Bún tôm rau cần Hải Phòng
fields: Nước dùng thơm tôm, vị dịu; tôm chín săn, mộc nhĩ giòn nhẹ và rau cần vừa chín tới.
Bún tôm rau cần Hải Phòng

Bún tôm Hải Phòng có nước dùng trong ngọt từ xương và đầu tôm, đi cùng tôm xào, mộc nhĩ, rau cần, cà chua và thì là. Bếp Việt biên tập lượng gia vị vừa cho bữa nhà; giữ phần tôm nguyên con lẫn tôm băm để tô bún có nhiều lớp vị.
Chần bún, xếp tôm và rau cần vào tô rồi chan nước dùng nóng. Rắc hành lá, thì là, tiêu; dọn chanh và ớt riêng.
4 tô bún tôm chan nước dùng xương và nước ngọt lọc từ đầu tôm.
Khoảng 1 giờ 15 phút, gồm thời gian ninh nước dùng.
Xào đầu và vỏ tôm đến khi dậy mùi rồi lọc kỹ để nước dùng thơm mà không lợn cợn.
Không nấu rau cần lâu; chần nhanh để giữ màu và độ giòn.
Nếu dùng nước mắm có độ mặn cao, nêm sau khi nước dùng đã cô vị.
Rau thơm và phần ăn kèm

names: Nha Trang jellyfish and fish noodle soup
ingredients: Cá liệt hoặc cá biển nhỏ
Sứa ăn liền đã sơ chế
fields: Nước dùng trong, ngọt thanh từ cá; sứa còn giòn, chả cá nóng và rau sống tươi mát.
Nha Trang jellyfish and fish noodle soup

Bún sứa Nha Trang gây nhớ bởi sứa biển trắng trong giòn sần sật, chả cá dai thơm và nước dùng thanh nấu từ cá liệt hoặc xương cá. Bếp Việt biên tập theo hướng nước trong, vị cá rõ; dùng sứa thực phẩm đã sơ chế và nêm mắm ruốc ở mức vừa.
Chần bún, xếp sứa và chả cá vào tô, chan nước dùng nóng. Dọn cùng giá, rau thơm, chanh, ớt và chén mắm ruốc để nêm theo khẩu vị.
4 tô bún sứa với chả cá, nước dùng cá biển trong và rau ghém.
Khoảng 1 giờ 25 phút, phần lớn là thời gian ninh nước dùng.
Chọn cá liệt hoặc cá biển tươi ít xương dăm; hớt bọt thường xuyên để nước dùng trong.
Dùng sứa đã sơ chế theo nhãn, trụng nhanh nếu sản phẩm yêu cầu; không đun lâu vì sứa sẽ teo và mất độ giòn.
Nêm mắm ruốc từng chút một, dọn riêng để giữ vị thanh cho nước dùng.
Cá liệt hoặc cá biển nhỏ
Sứa ăn liền đã sơ chế
Rau thơm và phần ăn kèm

names: Bánh xèo củ hủ dừa Bến Tre
Bánh xèo nhân củ hủ dừa
Bánh xèo tép củ hủ dừa Bến Tre
fields: Vỏ bánh mỏng giòn rìa, nhân tôm thịt vừa chín và củ hủ dừa còn độ giòn; rau ăn kèm làm vị bánh nhẹ hơn.
Bánh xèo nhân củ hủ dừa
Bánh xèo tép củ hủ dừa Bến Tre

Bánh xèo củ hủ dừa Bến Tre kết hợp lớp vỏ gạo vàng giòn với củ hủ dừa non giòn ngọt, tôm và thịt ba chỉ; nước cốt dừa làm phần bột thơm béo nhẹ. Bếp Việt biên tập công thức gia đình, giữ củ hủ dừa làm điểm nhấn và dọn cùng rau vườn, nước mắm chua ngọt.
Gấp bánh thành nửa trăng, dọn nóng cùng xà lách, rau thơm và chén nước mắm chua ngọt. Cuốn từng miếng với rau để cân vị béo.
4 bánh xèo cỡ vừa nhân tôm, thịt và củ hủ dừa, ăn kèm rau sống.
Khoảng 1 giờ, gồm thời gian chuẩn bị và đổ từng bánh.
bánh xèo củ hủ dừa Bến Tre
bánh xèo tép củ hủ dừa
Bánh xèo củ hủ dừa Bến Tre
Để bột nghỉ ít nhất 15 phút rồi khuấy lại trước khi đổ.
Củ hủ dừa nên cắt mỏng vừa để nhanh chín nhưng vẫn giòn.
Làm nóng chảo trước, tráng lớp bột mỏng và không đổ quá nhiều nhân để rìa bánh giòn.
Rau thơm và phần ăn kèm

names: Cá trích tái chanh Phú Quốc
Gỏi cá trích cuốn bánh tráng
ingredients: Cá trích phi lê ăn sống
Rau thơm và rau rừng ăn được
fields: Cá mát dịu vị chanh, dừa bào béo nhẹ, rau rừng thơm và nước mắm chua ngọt tạo cuốn gỏi cân vị.
Cá trích tái chanh Phú Quốc
Gỏi cá trích cuốn bánh tráng

Gỏi cá trích Phú Quốc là món cá tái chanh cuốn bánh tráng cùng rau rừng, khế, dừa bào và đậu phộng, chấm nước mắm cốt pha tỏi ớt. Bếp Việt biên tập phần ăn tại nhà và thêm chỉ dẫn chọn, giữ lạnh cá an toàn; nước chanh không thay thế quy trình kiểm soát ký sinh trùng của cá ăn sống.
Đặt miếng cá lên bánh tráng dầu dừa, thêm rau, khế, dừa bào và lạc rang, cuốn gọn rồi chấm nước mắm chua ngọt. Dọn cá lạnh và ăn ngay sau khi trộn.
4 phần gỏi cá trích tái chanh, cuốn với rau rừng, dừa bào và bánh tráng.
Khoảng 55 phút, gồm sơ chế và làm lạnh cá ngắn trước khi dọn.
Chỉ dùng cá từ nguồn có kiểm soát, được bán rõ ràng cho mục đích ăn sống; giữ lạnh liên tục và sơ chế bằng dụng cụ sạch.
Nước cốt chanh tạo vị tái nhưng không loại bỏ chắc chắn vi khuẩn hoặc ký sinh trùng; người mang thai, trẻ nhỏ, người cao tuổi hoặc suy giảm miễn dịch nên chọn cá đã nấu chín.
Cuốn bánh tráng dầu dừa không cần nhúng nước; nếu loại bánh tráng khô cứng, làm mềm theo hướng dẫn của nhà sản xuất.
Cá trích phi lê ăn sống

names: Phan Thiet Lau Tha Hot Pot
fields: A fragrant shrimp broth with gentle acidity from tomato and pineapple; ca mai, pork, egg and greens are arranged separately for cooking at the table.
Lâm Đồng (Phan Thiết, Bình Thuận cũ)

Lẩu thả Phan Thiết nổi bật với cá mai tươi và các nguyên liệu được bày riêng quanh nồi nước dùng. Bếp Việt biên tập phiên bản ăn nóng tại nhà, giữ cách bày nhiều thành phần và vị thanh từ tôm, cà chua, dứa.

Arrange vermicelli, greens, cucumber, pork, egg and ca mai on separate plates. Once the broth boils, cook the fish until opaque, then eat with noodles and greens; add a little sweet-and-sour sauce and roasted peanuts.
Four servings, with ca mai, vermicelli and greens arranged separately around a pot of hot broth.
Cá mai nên được giữ lạnh sau khi sơ chế và nhúng chín trong nước dùng đang sôi trước khi ăn.
lẩu thả cá mai Phan Thiết
cá mai ăn với bún rau
Phan Thiet Lau Tha Hot Pot
Choose very fresh ca mai, clean it thoroughly and keep it chilled; use a separate board and knife for raw fish.
Bring the broth to a steady boil before serving so the fish can cook through when dipped.
Add the dipping sauce gradually so it does not overpower the fish and greens.

names: Ca Mau Water-Sprite Shoots Stir-Fried with Tiny Shrimp
Đọt choại xào tép U Minh
fields: Fresh green, lightly crisp shoots coated with sweet shrimp, fragrant garlic and a touch of pepper.
Đọt choại xào tép U Minh
Đọt choại non xoắn nhẹ được xào nhanh với tép, tỏi và gia vị. Tuổi Trẻ ghi nhận đây là cách chế biến phổ biến ở vùng U Minh; Bếp Việt chuẩn hóa lượng nguyên liệu cho bữa cơm gia đình.
Serve hot with steamed rice. A small bowl of gently sweet, sour and spicy fish sauce is an optional accompaniment.
One family-style dish for four, served with rice.
Làm sạch rau và tép trước khi bật bếp; món xào nhanh sẽ giữ được độ giòn của đọt non.
đọt choại xào tép U Minh
món rau xào tép Cà Mau
Ca Mau Water-Sprite Shoots Stir-Fried with Tiny Shrimp
Choose fresh young shoots and remove old leaves and fibrous stems.
Add the shoots as soon as the shrimp turn golden and stir-fry briefly to retain their texture.
If the shoots are very mucilaginous, blanch them quickly and drain thoroughly before stir-frying.

names: Cao Bang Banh Khao (Pressed Glutinous Rice Cakes)
fields: Small ivory-colored cakes with fragrant, airy toasted-rice flour and a lightly sweet filling of peanuts, sesame and pork fat.
Bánh khảo là bánh Tết quen thuộc của người Tày, Nùng ở Cao Bằng, làm từ nếp rang xay mịn và nhân lạc, vừng, mỡ lợn. Bếp Việt biên tập cách làm gia đình với khuôn sạch và thời gian nghỉ bột ngắn.
Let the cakes set in the mold, then release and cut into small pieces. Serve with hot tea and store in an airtight container in a cool, dry place.
About 12 small cakes, two or three pieces per person.
Bột cần nguội hẳn sau khi rang và xay; lượng nước trộn phụ thuộc độ khô của bột nên thêm từ từ.
bánh khảo Tày Nùng Cao Bằng
Cao Bang Banh Khao (Pressed Glutinous Rice Cakes)
Toast the glutinous rice over low heat, stirring continuously so it turns aromatic without darkening.
Mill the rice very finely and sift it for a smooth, compact cake.
Rest the cakes in a clean mold lined with food-safe paper; never place the flour directly on the floor.

names: Ninh Binh Crispy Rice with Goat Sauce
Cơm cháy ăn kèm sốt thịt dê
fields: A golden, airy rice cake topped with lightly thickened goat sauce, tomato and mushrooms; the meat is tender and fragrant with ginger and lemongrass.
Ninh Bình (khu vực Ninh Bình cũ)
Cơm cháy ăn kèm sốt thịt dê
Cơm cháy Ninh Bình có lớp cơm vàng giòn từ nồi đáy dày; khi dùng có thể ăn cùng ruốc hoặc sốt thịt dê. Phiên bản Bếp Việt nấu sốt dê cà chua, nấm theo khẩu vị gia đình và phục vụ ngay trên cơm cháy.
Spoon only enough hot goat sauce over the crispy rice just before eating to keep the exposed surface crisp. Serve hot with herbs or pickled vegetables.
Four servings, each with a crisp rice cake and hot goat sauce.
Thời gian hong khô có thể thay đổi theo độ dày và độ ẩm của cơm; lớp cơm phải se khô trước khi chiên.
cơm cháy sốt dê Ninh Bình
cơm cháy đặc sản Ninh Bình
cơm cháy ăn với thịt dê
Ninh Binh Crispy Rice with Goat Sauce
Use a cast-iron or heavy-bottomed pot and keep the rice layer thin so the crust browns evenly.
Dry the rice crust before frying; this helps it puff and reduces oil splatter.
Add the sauce just before serving to keep the rice crisp.

names: Ngu Xa Pho Rolls from Ha Noi
Phở cuốn thịt bò Ngũ Xã
fields: Soft white pho sheets filled with fragrant garlic beef, lettuce and herbs, served with balanced sweet-and-sour dipping sauce.
Phở cuốn thịt bò Ngũ Xã
Bánh phở bản lớn cuốn thịt bò xào và rau thơm, ăn cùng nước mắm pha chua ngọt là món quen thuộc ở Ngũ Xã, Hà Nội. Bếp Việt biên tập định lượng dễ làm tại nhà, giữ phần nhân gọn để cuốn không bung.
Arrange the rolls on a platter with a bowl of sweet-and-sour fish sauce with garlic and chili. Serve while the beef is aromatic and the pho sheets are soft.
About 16 rolls, suitable for four light servings or two to three main-meal servings.
Để thịt nguội bớt trước khi cuốn; bánh phở mềm dễ rách nếu nhân còn quá nóng hoặc quá ướt.
phở cuốn thịt bò Hà Nội
Ngu Xa Pho Rolls from Ha Noi
Choose wide pho sheets that are soft but not overly wet so the rolls hold their shape.
Let the beef cool slightly before rolling to keep the pho sheets from tearing.
Do not overfill; place the greens in the middle and roll snugly.

names: Quang Ngai Tra River Goby Braised with Pepper
Cá bống kho tiêu sông Trà
Cá bống kho tiêu Quảng Ngãi
fields: Whole gobies are firm and peppery, coated in a light glossy sauce fragrant with shallot.
Cá bống kho tiêu sông Trà
Cá bống kho tiêu Quảng Ngãi

Cá bống nhỏ được kho liu riu với nước mắm, tiêu và chút ớt đến khi săn chắc, bóng màu cánh gián. Bếp Việt biên tập cách nấu gọn cho bữa cơm nhà, giữ điểm nhấn tiêu thơm và vị mặn ngọt vừa phải của cá bống sông Trà.
Serve hot with steamed rice and boiled greens; spoon a little braising sauce over the rice.
One small pot of fish served with steamed rice for four.
Cá càng nhỏ càng nhanh thấm; tránh kho cạn khô để thịt cá không xác.
Quang Ngai Tra River Goby Braised with Pepper
Choose fresh small gobies; rinse gently and drain well so they stay intact.
Season with fish sauce early, then taste near the end because the sauce will reduce.
Braise over low heat and gently shake the pot instead of stirring.
Soft rice grains in a lightly thickened broth, with plump oysters and fragrant pepper and herbs.
TP. Hồ Chí Minh (Bà Rịa - Vũng Tàu cũ)

Gạo nấu nhừ thành cháo sánh nhẹ, hàu được xào nhanh rồi cho vào gần cuối để giữ vị ngọt biển. Hành phi, hành lá, rau mùi và tiêu làm bát cháo thơm ấm; công thức Bếp Việt được biên tập theo khẩu vị gia đình.
Ladle into bowls and finish with fried shallot, scallion, cilantro and pepper; thinly sliced banana blossom is optional.
Thời gian ninh phụ thuộc loại gạo; hàu nên thêm vào cuối và nấu chín vừa đủ.
Use cleaned oysters kept properly chilled, and cook through.
Sauté oysters just until firm and add near the end to avoid a rubbery texture.
Add hot water if porridge thickens, and stir the bottom regularly.

names: Vegetarian Braised Young Jackfruit with Straw Mushrooms
Mít non kho nấm và đậu hũ
fields: Tender jackfruit with sweet mushrooms and tofu in a lightly reduced lemongrass sauce.
Mít non kho nấm và đậu hũ
Mít non có thớ bùi, được kho cùng nấm rơm và đậu hũ trong nước tương, sả và nước mắm chay. Công thức Bếp Việt biên tập để phần sốt sánh vừa và nguyên liệu vẫn giữ dáng.
Serve with rice and cilantro or leek greens. Check seasonings are plant-based for a fully vegan meal.
One shared braise for a four-person meal.
Mít non tươi và mít sơ chế sẵn có độ mềm khác nhau; điều chỉnh thời gian để miếng mít không nát.
Vegetarian Braised Young Jackfruit with Straw Mushrooms
If fresh jackfruit is sticky with latex, boil it for 5 minutes and drain before pan-frying.
Briefly pan-frying jackfruit and tofu helps the pieces hold their shape.
Use vegetarian fish sauce; do not use regular fish sauce for a vegetarian meal.

names: Cha ca La Vong (turmeric fish with dill)
Chả cá thì là Hà Nội
fields: Golden turmeric fish fragrant with galangal and fermented rice, tossed with dill and scallion and served with vermicelli, peanuts and seasoned shrimp paste.
Cha ca La Vong (turmeric fish with dill)
Chả cá thì là Hà Nội

Cá lăng ướp riềng, nghệ và mẻ được làm chín hai lượt để ngoài vàng thơm, trong vẫn mềm; khi ăn đảo nóng cùng thì là và hành. Bếp Việt biên tập cách làm tại nhà, linh hoạt dùng lò nướng hoặc nồi chiên trước khi hoàn thiện trên chảo.
Bring the pan to the table and serve with vermicelli, peanuts, herbs and lime-chili shrimp paste.
Four portions served with vermicelli, herbs and peanuts.
Giữ lạnh cá trong thời gian ướp; độ chín phụ thuộc độ dày miếng và thiết bị.

In an air fryer or oven, arrange fish in one layer and cook just until done; do not dry it out.
Fermented rice varies in acidity, so taste the marinade before adding lime or vinegar.
Add dill and scallion at the end so they wilt but keep their color.

names: Quang Nam Banh Thuan Flower Cakes
fields: Pale golden cakes bloom into petals, smell of egg and have a lightly dry exterior with an airy crumb.

Bánh thuẫn xứ Quảng có cánh nở như hoa, thơm trứng và thường được làm dịp Tết, giỗ hoặc để mời khách. Bếp Việt biên tập mẻ nhỏ dùng bột bình tinh, trứng và đường, nướng bằng khuôn nhỏ tại nhà; cấu trúc bánh tùy loại bột và khuôn.
Cool on a rack and serve with hot tea; store airtight once completely cool.
About 12 small cakes, depending on mold size.

Quang Nam Banh Thuan Flower Cakes
Sift arrowroot starch and beat eggs thoroughly for a smooth batter.

fields: Sticky rice seeds are soft and naturally pink and purple; The meat is soft and fleshy, has a mild sour taste and a characteristic aroma.
Cao Bang Glutinous Rice with Black Canarium

Cao Bang black canarium sticky rice is an autumn specialty: softened black canarium flesh is pitted and folded into hot sticky rice, coloring the grains mauve and adding a gentle, nutty richness. Bep Viet adapts it for a family-sized batch and keeps the fruit-softening step separate to prevent a tough or astringent result.
Serve hot in a bowl or tray lined with clean leaves. You can sprinkle sesame salt or roasted peanuts; Traditional dishes can also be eaten with minced meat depending on the region and taste.
4 servings of black sticky rice, served hot; Can be used with sesame salt.

sticky rice filled with sticky rice

names: Lang Son Khau Nhuc (Braised Pork Belly Dome)
fields: The pork belly is soft and absorbent, the shiny brown skin, the fleshy taro and the fragrant salty shrimp create a bold but round flavor.

Khau nhuc, also called nam khau, is a labor-intensive steamed dish associated with the Tay and Nung communities of Lang Son, often served for family celebrations and weddings. Bep Viet adapts the process for a home kitchen: brown the pork skin, layer the pork with taro and preserved mustard greens, then steam slowly until tender.
Place the steaming bowl on a deep plate, sprinkle the steaming liquid on top and serve hot with white rice, bread or boiled vegetables.
The 6 parts include steamed pork belly, taro and seasoned pork belly.
About 6:15 a.m.; Mostly slow steaming time to soften the meat.
Lang Son Khau Nhuc (Braised Pork Belly Dome)
Choose pork belly with balanced layers of lean, fat and skin; Prick the skin evenly to let the seasoning absorb.
Pat the skin dry before sautéing; Place the skin side down in the hot oil and cover to avoid splashing.
Chinese soi is quite salty, so taste it before adding salt or soy sauce; Steam over low heat and add hot water as needed.
Hot fish smells of roasted mushrooms and guava leaves, firm fibers, mild sour and salty taste; Grill until the fish is not dry.

Lap Thach fermented fish is a traditional way of preserving fish from the Lo River with salt, toasted corn meal and guava leaves, producing a distinctive tangy aroma. Bep Viet adapts it as a quick grilled dish and uses only fully fermented fish from a trusted producer; it does not provide instructions for fermenting raw fish at home.
Grill thoroughly, remove the meat and eat with white rice, herbs and cucumbers. Do not eat raw or undercooked fish.
4 portions of fish are completely fermented, grilled and eaten with hot rice.
About 32 minutes if using fully fermented fish; Traditional incubation times are not included in this recipe.
Choose fish products with clear labels, origin and preservation instructions.
Do not ferment raw fish at home without procedures to control salt, temperature and time.
If the fish is salty, serve with rice and boiled vegetables; No need to add salty dipping sauce.

The cake crust is clear and golden; The green bean filling is soft and fleshy, with grated coconut and fragrant lotus seeds.

Dinh Bang husband-and-wife cake is known for its translucent golden glutinous-rice shell, lightly crisp green papaya strands and sweet mung-bean and coconut filling. Bep Viet adapts a small home batch while retaining the traditional two-layer leaf wrapping and natural gardenia coloring.
Let the cake cool down, then serve it whole or cut it in half to reveal the clear crust and filling. Store cool in an airtight container and use within a day.
6 husband and wife cakes wrapped in leaves, used as sweets or holiday gifts.
About 2 hours 35 minutes, not including time for cake to cool completely.
Dinh Bang bride and groom cake
Squeeze out the water from the papaya after grating it so that the skin doesn't become mushy.
Stir the flour continuously over low heat until it thickens, avoiding the bottom of the pot being sharp.
Wrap the leaves tightly in your hand, do not press too tightly so that the dough has room to expand when steamed.

names: Vegetarian Sang Greens and Mushroom Soup
fields: Clear, sweet soup from mushrooms; Soft green spinach leaves, tofu and mushrooms create a light feeling in the stomach.
Vegetarian Sang Greens and Mushroom Soup

Sang greens are a forest vegetable associated with Xuan Son, Phu Tho, with tender young leaves and a naturally sweet finish; local versions are cooked with pork, shrimp or fish. Bep Viet offers a clearly labeled vegetarian adaptation with mushrooms and tofu, letting the greens remain the main flavor.
Ladle the soup while it's still hot, serve with white rice and vegetarian stew. Do not boil vegetables for long to preserve color and tenderness.
4 bowls of vegetable soup with mushrooms in the vegetarian version edited by Bep Viet.
About 33 minutes, cook quickly so the vegetables retain their green color and sweetness.
Only pick or buy vegetables of clear origin; Choose young leaves, avoid mixing with unidentified forest trees.
Wash gently several times and drain; The old stems can be put in the pot before the leaves.
Season with soy sauce or salt moderately to not overwhelm the natural sweetness of the vegetables and mushrooms.

names: Chè lam Thạch Xá Hà Nội
fields: Chewy, firm pieces lightly dusted with rice flour; molasses sweetness is balanced by warm ginger and nutty peanuts.
Chè lam Thạch Xá Hà Nội

Chè lam Thạch Xá là thức quà xứ Đoài làm từ bột nếp rang, mật mía, gừng và lạc rang. Bếp Việt biên tập mẻ nhỏ tại nhà, cân bằng độ dẻo và vị cay ấm; tỷ lệ không đại diện cho công thức của một hộ làng nghề.
Let the cake cool completely, cut into bite-size pieces and serve with green or hot tea.

Add toasted rice flour gradually so the mixture stays chewy rather than dry and crumbly.
Cook molasses over low heat, stirring constantly to prevent scorching.
Fold in the peanuts last to keep them crisp.

names: Khoai xéo khoai khô Hà Tĩnh
fields: Soft dried sweet potato and sticky rice combine with beans and peanuts for a gently sweet, nutty dish that is not mushy.
Khoai xéo khoai khô Hà Tĩnh

Khoai xéo là món ăn dân dã Hà Tĩnh từ khoai lang thái lát phơi khô, nấu cùng nếp, đậu và lạc. Bếp Việt biên tập cách nấu gia đình có ngâm đậu trước để hạt chín mềm, sau đó xéo nhẹ để món dẻo bùi mà vẫn còn thớ khoai.
Serve warm as breakfast or a snack; add a little sesame-peanut salt if desired.
One pot of chewy, nutty khoai xeo for four people.
Khoảng 7 giờ 10 phút, chủ yếu là thời gian ngâm đậu; có thể ngâm từ tối hôm trước.
Soak dry beans and cook until tender before adding the rice.
Keep the water just level with the ingredients after adding rice; add hot water little by little if needed.
Mash lightly while hot, leaving some sweet potato pieces and beans intact.

Quickly sear the beef in a hot pan, remove it, and return it at the end to keep it tender.
Season lightly because the pan juices concentrate as they reduce.

ingredients: Young mac khen leaves or fresh herbs
fields: The soup is lightly thickened by softened rice, with tender chicken, delicate young banana pith and fragrant lemongrass.

Canh ột là món canh gạo và rau thơm của cộng đồng người Thái miền Tây Nghệ An; có nhiều biến thể theo nguyên liệu chính. Bếp Việt biên tập phiên bản gà cho gia đình, dùng lõi chuối non, sả và gạo ngâm giã dập; đây không phải công thức đại diện cho mọi bản hoặc gia đình.

The fish is fully cooked with lightly charred skin, firm sweet flesh and a fragrant aroma.

fields: The pastry is golden and crisp, with a soft pork, mushroom and noodle filling and a quail egg inside.
Bánh gối phố cổ Hà Nội

Hanoi bánh gối is a crisp, pillow-shaped pastry filled with minced pork, wood-ear mushroom, glass noodles and quail egg. This Bếp Việt home batch cools and drains the filling before sealing and frying.
Serve hot with fresh greens, green papaya pickles and sweet-sour fish sauce.

wood-ear mushroom and glass noodle pastry
Cool and drain the filling before wrapping.

names: Hanoi Rice Noodle Soup with Taro Stems
fields: The broth is clear and balanced; the pork is tender, the meatballs savory and the taro stems crisp without an itchy afterfeel.

This Hanoi bowl pairs a light broth with tender pork hock, wood-ear meatballs and crisp taro stems. Bếp Việt’s home recipe explains how to salt, squeeze and rinse the stems to reduce their itchy sensation.
Briefly blanch the noodles, arrange the pork and meatballs, ladle over hot broth and finish with scallion, culantro and cilantro.
Four bowls of rice noodles with pork, meatballs and clear broth.
A gentle simmer keeps the broth clear; salt and rinse the taro stems thoroughly before cooking.

Wear gloves when handling taro stems if your skin is sensitive; salt, squeeze and rinse them several times.

Blanch the taro stems only until just tender; prolonged cooking removes their crisp texture.

names: Giong Luong Coconut Leaf Cake from Ben Tre
fields: Golden-green leaves enclose tender sticky rice with nutty black beans, ripe banana and a gentle coconut aroma.

Giong Luong cake is wrapped in young nipa palm leaves and combines chewy sticky rice with coconut, black beans and ripe banana. Bếp Việt adapts the long-standing Thạnh Phú craft for a small home batch; wrapping and extended steaming take patience.
Let the parcels cool slightly, unwrap and serve whole or sliced; best eaten the day they are made.
This recipe keeps the extended steaming time documented for the traditional craft; actual time varies with parcel thickness.
Ben Tre nipa palm leaf cake

Soak the sticky rice long enough and drain it thoroughly so the cake cooks chewy rather than wet.
Wipe the young nipa leaves clean, roll them into sealed tubes and tie firmly to keep water out.
Steam for the full time; for larger or thicker parcels, check the center before turning off the heat.

fields: Smooth, chewy white sticky rice surrounds a nutty mung-bean and savory pork filling with a light banana-leaf aroma.

Quán Gánh bánh dày is a well-known sticky-rice cake from Thường Tín, Hanoi. This Bếp Việt savory version combines pounded sticky rice with mung bean and pork filling, wrapped in banana leaf.

Eight savory bánh dày cakes wrapped in banana leaf, for four people.

Oil your hands lightly to prevent sticking.

names: Northern Vietnamese Rice Balls with Sesame Salt
fields: The rice holds together while staying soft and chewy; the sesame salt is fragrant, nutty and mildly salty, with optional roasted peanuts.

Warm rice is pressed into a tender, chewy roll and served with nutty toasted sesame salt, a humble countryside food from northern Vietnam. Bếp Việt keeps the method simple and explains how to cook rice that binds well and shape it while warm.
Slice the rice roll with a slightly wet knife or clean thread and dip into sesame salt while still warm.
Four servings of rice balls with sesame salt, for breakfast or a packed meal.

This Hue lagoon specialty pairs small rabbitfish with a thin rice-flour batter, bean sprouts and scallions. Bep Viet adapts it for a family kitchen, keeping the fish at the center and seasoning it lightly to accompany the dipping sauce.

Golden grilled skewers smell of lemongrass and remain tender; serve with herbs, green banana, cucumber, noodles and dipping sauce.

Huế nem lụi are seasoned ground meat wrapped around lemongrass stalks and grilled, commonly eaten as rolls with rice paper, noodles and herbs. This Bếp Việt batch adds shrimp and pork fat for a juicy texture.

The eggplant is soft but still in pieces, the tofu is soaked in soy sauce, the stock is light and fragrant with pepper.

Tender eggplant and lightly fried tofu are gently braised with soy sauce and black pepper for an easy, home-style vegetarian meal. Bep Viet keeps the braising liquid light enough to coat the ingredients, with optional leek and chili for aroma without excess salt.

Bánh tai yến nước cốt dừa

Bánh tai yến is a Mekong Delta snack with a flared rim resembling a bird’s nest, made with rice flour, tapioca starch, coconut milk and sugar. This Bếp Việt batch rests the batter before frying individual cakes.

Rest the batter for about 4 hours, as described in the cultural reference.

Pour a modest amount into hot oil so the rim flares and center puffs.

names: Khmer Ginger Cake from Sóc Trăng
fields: Ginger-root shapes have a crisp, airy shell with a white sugar coating and a sweet, rich rice-and-egg flavor.

Bánh gừng, called Num-khơ-nhây in Khmer, is a traditional Khmer Southern Vietnamese cake served during festivals, holidays and celebrations in Sóc Trăng. Sticky-rice flour and egg dough is shaped like ginger roots, fried and coated with sugar.
Let dry completely and serve with tea; store airtight in a dry place.
About 12 small ginger-shaped cakes coated with crystallized sugar.

Do not drop the cakes into very hot oil; it can harden them before they rise.
Fry until golden and firm, then drain before glazing.
Stir gently in the glaze until sugar turns white and crystallizes on the cakes.

Blanch noodles separately to keep the broth clear and noodles firm.

fields: A fragrant, savory-sweet broth with a gentle reddish-brown hue, tender springy shrimp suông, pork, shrimp and crisp fresh greens.
